title: Performance Marketing Manager
description:
Why we do what we do

The mind is our window to the world. It can paint everything outside in grey or in bright colors. Whoever finds access to that window can change their perspective every day, and psychological hurdles can become chances to grow. Happiness spreads from one person to the next and across a whole society, like a quiet revolution, one mind at a time.

Who we are

Our mission inspires us and challenges us. Our skills, thoughts and ideas go into a product that reaches thousands of people, and that brings responsibility with it. The work asks for passion, integrity and the courage to try things no one has tried before.

A team full of people who are crazy enough to think they can change the world they live in. Yes, we are a hardworking team, but not for us alone, not for money or personal fame, but for the people we serve at the center of our efforts: Our team, clients, psychologists on our platform and supporters across the country.

Why this role exists

Aepsy serves three audiences, each with its own timeline. Clients need support now. Psychologists are building their practice. Employers are deciding whether to unlock access for their whole team.

This role leads performance marketing for all three: how people find Aepsy, what actually works, and what the numbers suggest we do next.

Marketing at Aepsy is a small, focused team, and every role has a clear place in it. The Creative Marketing Lead owns copy and shapes the campaigns. The Art Director builds the visual language. The Growth Performance Architect owns the measurement architecture. You work closely with all three, bringing campaigns to the right people through the right channels, finding out what worked, and helping the team decide what to keep, change or stop.

Performance with principles

Our values shape how we advertise. Privacy is non-negotiable. Anyone visiting a mental health platform deserves the highest level of privacy and data security. That means no urgency or fear in our messages, no before-and-after claims, and no targeting or retargeting based on health data or other sensitive personal information.

Sometimes this makes a number harder to reach. It also builds trust that lasts, and that trust is why people choose Aepsy. If strong performance combined with strong principles sounds like the challenge you’ve been looking for, we’d love to hear from you.

What you’ll do

  • Own performance across all funnels. Clients may decide within days. Employers take longer and involve several people. Together with the colleagues closest to each audience, you define what success means for each one.

  • Run paid media end to end on Meta, Google, TikTok and LinkedIn. That covers structure, bidding, audiences, creative rotation, and both awareness and conversion, plus the judgement to know which of the two you’re working on.

  • Read the numbers and get more out of them. The Growth Performance Architect builds the measurement setup with you. You turn it into insights the team can act on.

  • Turn patterns into decisions. Why do people who considered Aepsy drop off before deciding? Does the response to a creative suggest it should run weekly rather than monthly? Answering questions like these is the core of the role.

  • Shape how people find support. Search is changing fast, and new ways of discovering things are emerging. You’ll help decide how people find Aepsy when they need it most.

  • Help build the team’s marketing rhythm. You’ll set up the flow for campaigns, newsletters and more, from first idea to delivery, so the whole team can rely on it.

What you bring

  • Three to four years in performance marketing, including campaigns you’ve run end to end and at least one that didn’t go as planned and taught you something.

  • A data-driven mindset with a real feel for brand and content.

  • Confidence running Meta and Google on your own, and experience with TikTok or LinkedIn for reaching HR leads and psychologists. Bring the channels you’ve found work best.

  • Judgement that weighs data together with values. The field is sensitive, Switzerland is a small multilingual market, and the mission matters.

  • Fluent (Swiss) German and English. Aepsy works in four languages, German is the largest market, and most partners and HR leads communicate in German.

  • A habit of noticing a step that repeats and improving it, using AI in your daily work.

Strongly preferred

  • SEO and GEO basics, and curiosity about how AI search engines choose which sources to cite.

  • Lifecycle marketing experience: segmentation, triggers and deliverability.

  • Experience at an organisation with strong convictions, and enjoyment of doing great work within clear principles.

What we offer

  • Work that matters. Every campaign you improve helps someone find support a little sooner. Your skills serve something bigger than a conversion rate.

  • A team that has your back. The Creative Marketing Lead, Art Director, Growth Performance Architect and Head of Marketing are each strong in their field. You’ll never have to face a number alone.

  • A strong foundation. You’ll build on a product people trust, a network of qualified psychologists, partnerships with employers and insurers, and values clear enough to make hard decisions easier.

  • Room to shape things. There are three audiences, several funnels, a content area being rebuilt, and a search landscape that AI is changing. Your ideas will have impact, and you’ll see it.

  • A short line to decisions. You’ll report directly to the Head of Marketing and have access to leadership strategy.

  • Modern tools, including AI, and the freedom to use them well.

  • Time to recharge: five weeks of holiday and a mental health benefit (of course).

Together with us

We’re a young, ambitious team with diverse backgrounds and beliefs. We love conversations about the big picture and about the small details. We believe in what we do and work hard for a slightly better world. We’re also friends, parents, partners, stand-up comedians, yoga beginners and Zen monks who enjoy life.

Sleep on it. Read it again. Then take a deep breath and send us:

  • Your CV and a personal cover letter. We read every letter carefully, so tell us what motivates you, why this mission matters to you, and why this role, right now.

  • Whatever shows your thinking best. A short note is enough. One campaign you can explain well is worth more than a full portfolio.

In our conversation we’ll be curious about two things: a number that proved you wrong, and something you decided to stop doing.

PS: Please skip the generic, AI-generated cover letter. A few honest lines in your own words mean much more to us. The time you save is better spent in the sun, on a walk in the forest or with a friend. Life is too beautiful for impersonal cover letters :)

Over ons

De halfgeleiderindustrie vraagt om steeds krachtigere chips: meer bandbreedte, minder energieverbruik. Onze technologie levert precies dat. Wij verbinden chips met computernetwerken die enorme hoeveelheden data verwerken, met minimale vertraging. Samen veranderen we de manier waarop de wereld met elkaar verbonden is.

In Zoetermeer werkt ons grafeenteam aan de toekomst van de halfgeleiderindustrie, van onderzoek en ontwikkeling tot industrialisatie. Die processen vormen de basis van onze geïntegreerde grafeenfotonica. Het team pioniert met nieuwe procestechnologie en schaalt die op tot productierijpe oplossingen. Zo wordt baanbrekend onderzoek omgezet in de bouwstenen van de chips van morgen.

De functie

Black Semiconductor is op zoek naar een gemotiveerde Technicus (m/v/x) om ons team op locatie in Zoetermeer, Nederland, te versterken.

Je speelt een cruciale rol bij het waarborgen van de betrouwbare werking van alle technische systemen die onze cleanroomomgeving ondersteunen. Je bent verantwoordelijk voor onderhouds-, storingsanalyse- en reparatiewerkzaamheden aan voorzieningen zoals luchtbehandeling, gas-, water- en elektrische systemen. Deze functie is ideaal voor een praktisch ingestelde professional met technisch inzicht die graag zelfstandig werkt, technische uitdagingen oplost en nieuwe vaardigheden ontwikkelt in een sterk gecontroleerde en innovatieve omgeving.

  • Technische problemen diagnosticeren en oplossen om stilstand tot een minimum te beperken en de operationele continuïteit te waarborgen.

  • Onderhoudswerkzaamheden coördineren en uitvoeren, met inachtneming van normen en veiligheidsvoorschriften.

  • Verantwoordelijkheid nemen voor technische uitdagingen en proactief mogelijkheden identificeren voor systeemverbeteringen en een hogere betrouwbaarheid.

Jouw kwalificaties

  • Afgeronde beroepsopleiding in een mechanische, technische of onderhoud gerelateerde richting (bijvoorbeeld automonteur, industrieel monteur, mechatronicatechnicus of vergelijkbaar).

  • Praktische ervaring met mechanische systemen en basiskennis van elektrische, pneumatische, gas- of utiliteitssystemen.

  • Sterke hands-on mentaliteit met het vertrouwen om onbekende technische uitdagingen aan te pakken en nieuwe technologieën te leren.

  • Vermogen om zelfstandig te werken, prioriteiten te stellen en volledige verantwoordelijkheid te nemen voor toegewezen taken.

  • Probleemoplossende instelling, sterke vaardigheden in storingsanalyse en bereidheid om te werken in een cleanroomomgeving met strikte kwaliteits- en veiligheidsnormen.

  • Comfortabel met praktisch werk in cleanroom-, laboratorium- en facilitaire omgevingen, inclusief het gebruik van ladders om verhoogde gebieden te bereiken en het werken in beperkte ruimtes onder de cleanroom wanneer dat nodig is.

  • In staat om fysiek veeleisende onderhouds- en installatiewerkzaamheden veilig uit te voeren, zoals het vervangen van HEPA-filters, het bedienen van afsluiters, het positioneren van gascilinders en het verplaatsen van zware vacuümpompen. Voor zware lasten worden geschikte hulpmiddelen en ondersteuning van collega’s ingezet.

  • Sterke communicatieve vaardigheden in het Engels, bij voorkeur ook in het Nederlands om te kunnen communiceren met externe partijen, management en operators.

Ervaring in de halfgeleiderindustrie is niet vereist. Je ontvangt de nodige training en ondersteuning om de apparatuur te leren kennen en je technische vaardigheden verder te ontwikkelen.

Hoe succes eruitziet

  • Volledige verantwoordelijkheid nemen voor de cleanroominfrastructuur, en zorgen voor een betrouwbare werking van luchtbehandeling, gas-, water-, afzuig- en elektrische systemen met minimale stilstand.

  • Technische kennis en vaardigheden continu uitbreiden, snel nieuwe systemen en technologieën eigen maken en tegelijkertijd de hoge standaarden handhaven die vereist zijn binnen een cleanroomomgeving.

Onze werkcultuur

Mensen boven processen. Bij Black Semiconductor is flexibiliteit essentieel — wij zorgen ervoor dat werk zich aanpast aan het leven, en niet andersom. We stimuleren een gezonde balans tussen werk en privé, waarin carrières betekenisvol en verrijkend zijn. Onze processen zijn mensgericht, zodat jij je kunt richten op wat echt belangrijk is.

Jouw gezondheid en toekomst zijn belangrijk. Jouw welzijn heeft de hoogste prioriteit. Jouw gemoedsrust staat bij ons centraal — nu én in de toekomst.

Wij leven openheid. Samenwerking en inclusiviteit vormen de hoekstenen van onze cultuur. Wij geloven in openheid en bouwen aan vertrouwen en respect. Individualiteit is onze gezamenlijke kracht, die innovatie stimuleert en ons vooruit helpt.

Wij verbinden chips – en mensen. Wij moedigen gekwalificeerde kandidaten van iedere achtergrond aan om te solliciteren. We creëren een inclusieve en ondersteunende werkomgeving waarin samenwerking, innovatie en groei centraal staan. Sluit je aan bij ons team en maak deel uit van een organisatie die een verschil maakt in de industrie.

Why SDK Engineering at Langfuse

You will grow at Langfuse by

  • Owning our SDKs. We maintain SDKs in Python and TypeScript both built on OpenTelemetry. You'll be responsible for their reliability, performance, and developer experience. These SDKs run inside our users' production systems, which means they must never fail, must have minimal impact on CPU and memory, and must work flawlessly across every environment — from serverless functions to long-running agent loops. You'll think deeply about the exposed interfaces, error handling, batching, async flushing, and graceful degradation.

  • Designing APIs that developers love. How are functions named, how are parameters structured, how are breaking changes communicated, how does the documentation read? Developer experience is a core differentiator for Langfuse and you'll own every detail of it. When we shipped the Python SDK v3 and TypeScript SDK v4, both were full rewrites on OpenTelemetry — that's the kind of thoughtful, high-impact SDK work you'll lead. Apart from tracing, we also support core workflows of engineers building with LLMs with our SDKs, see our Experiment Runner SDK for example.

  • Integrating with every major AI framework: Langfuse integrates with 40+ frameworks and model providers: OpenAI SDK, Vercel AI SDK, AI SDK, LangChain, LlamaIndex, Pydantic AI, OpenAI Agents, CrewAI, Amazon Bedrock AgentCore, LiveKit, and many more. You'll maintain these integrations, ensure new Langfuse features are supported across all of them, and add new integrations as the ecosystem evolves. When a new framework gains traction, you'll be among the first to instrument it.

  • Maintaining our OpenTelemetry endpoint: some users send traces directly to our OTLP endpoint instead of using our SDKs. You'll ensure this path is robust, well-documented, and supports the full range of Langfuse features. This also extends our language support to Java, Go, and any language with an OpenTelemetry SDK. You can work with the OpenTelemetry community to steer the GenAI conventions.

  • Writing public documentation: you'll own the SDK docs, integration guides, and migration paths. At Langfuse, docs are part of our core product. When you ship a new SDK version or integration, the docs ship with it.

  • Strong engineer who gets excited about developer experience, API design, and writing code that runs reliably in other people's production systems

  • Experience building or maintaining SDKs, client libraries, or developer tools — ideally in Python and/or TypeScript

  • Deep understanding of performance: you know how to profile, benchmark, and minimize CPU/memory overhead in hot paths

  • Someone who can manage projects themselves — you know how to develop strong conviction about what to build and how to ship it

  • Drive & Motivation: Comfortable in fast-paced, high-ownership scale-up environments. You want to own outcomes, not backlogs, and you are excited to define what a premium hybrid private client experience looks like in an AI-native product organization.

What we offer

  • Diversity: Flat hierarchies and cultural openness make you an integral part of our diverse team of international talents from day one.

  • Flexibility: We don’t complicate your life. You’ll find the right balance with flexible work models, working hours, and remote work options. 28 days of vacation and two additional days off on December 24 and 31 ensure you have ample time to unwind.

We are LIQID, one of the fastest-growing fintechs in Europe. Our purpose is to provide creators, entrepreneurs, and thinkers shaping our future with access to the same opportunities as the world’s most successful investors while balancing the demands of people, planet, and profit.

description:
Few people get to build a bank from scratch. Even fewer get to build one at a moment when banking itself is being reinvented.


The Dollar is the best product in the history of the world - there is infinite global demand. But International Fintechs and non-US banks are left with two unsatisfying options to access it: Either they build on legacy clearing banks that are slow and unreliable, or they interface with middleware providers that don’t move and hold the dollars directly, but themselves rely on underlying legacy banks. Augustus collapses this stack by combining two things: A real, national bank charter (in organization), and Marble, our proprietary core banking system, built around intelligence, made of code.


We are a group of operators, unicorn early employees, ex-founders and people who walked away from degrees because they believe this is an industry and career defining opportunity. We are backed with more than $200M from Peter Thiel's Valar Ventures, Tiger Global, Hummingbird, QED, Creandum, and the founders of Nubank, Ramp, Deel, Circle, Fluidstack, Fuse, and n8n.


We are regulated in Europe and live with Euro and Stablecoin clearing today. Now, we are building the US team from the ground up, while continuing to grow rapidly in Europe.

The Role

You own Banking Experience: the accounts at the center of customer's relationship with the bank, and the API and dashboards they use to manage them.

In this role you’re responsible for redefining what beautiful software in banking looks like. You'll define account structures that give customers powerful building blocks for their products, and craft intuitive interfaces grounded in a deep understanding of their use cases and workflows.

You report to Will, Head of Product, and work closely with Simon, our CTO. You're expected to operate with full autonomy on your team's roadmap, collaborating with design and engineering.

  • Months 1-2: Take over day-to-day ownership of the Banking Experience team - the roadmap, the ways of working, the hard decisions. Establish yourself with customers and how they use our accounts. You define and ship your first project.

  • Months 3-4: Execution mode. You're unblocking engineering daily, making hard prioritization calls, and shipping your roadmap to customers. You're proactively raising the bar across accounts, API, and dashboard by feeding what you learn from customers into the product.

  • Months 5-6: You're working with live customers on the products you've built. Deposits and number of account holders are scaling. You've moved from execution to platform mode - evolving the roadmap based on what our customers are building on top of Augustus.

Who Will Thrive At Augustus

We believe that throwing smart people with high agency at big problems produces the best outcomes. We’re building a modern correspondent bank, and we win by having a better team. The people who succeed here share the following traits:

  • American Dream: You’d rather shoot for gold than settle for mediocrity. You pick the harder goal and stay optimistic when the odds are against you. If it feels easy, we aimed too low.

  • Live Player: You don’t need permission. You rebuild what’s broken without being asked, challenge how things are done, and move before the perfect moment.

  • Ever to Excel: You can’t accept good enough and you take your work personally. When it matters, you do what it takes and keep raising the bar for yourself and your team.

  • Genuine: You play for the company, not your title or turf. Low ego, low drama, no politics. You say it straight, also upwards and always assume good intent.

  • You combine first-principles thinking with deep domain knowledge to make complex processes simple.

  • You have taste and care deeply about the quality of what you build.

  • You leverage AI to push the boundaries of what a PM can do.

  • You’re excited about building a programmable bank and helping shape what that means.

Hard Requirements

  • Experience end-to-end owning and building banking, fintech, or developer platform products.

  • Technical enough to spar on architectural decisions with engineers - you're comfortable in API design discussions, not just UI reviews.

  • You have experience with control planes, dashboards, or console products at infrastructure, finance, or developer tools companies.

  • Comfortable in customer-facing roles - you've pitched, demoed, and closed early adopters yourself.

Pay transparency

Compensation packages at Augustus include base salary, equity, and benefits. New hire offers are made based on a candidate's experience, expertise and geographic location. The annual US base salary range for this role is $180,000-$230,000 + equity.

  • Career Growth: You will be given more responsibility and pushed to grow faster than ever before.

Join BLP and help make the world’s business processes autonomous!

Our agentic platform helps finance and operations teams worldwide remove manual work from their core business processes, so work runs end-to-end with greater control and significant productivity gains.

Join us and help make autonomous operations the new standard.

What the job actually feels like

This is a build job.

When you join, BLP has no UK pipeline, no UK case studies, and no local playbook. It’s not the well-oiled machine with sophisticated processes for everything. What you get instead: an experienced Account Executive sitting next to you, a reporting line to the VP of Business Development and a strong DACH SDR team behind you. You get a winning product and a market nobody here has sold into yet. All of that comes with strong support from the Switzerland HQ.


Your first job is to work out who buys, why, and what makes them pick up the phone. You will hear no far more often than yes. The yes is a 30-minute discovery call with a CFO, COO, or Head of Finance at a large UK manufacturer or industrial business, where you run the meeting, present the value, and map the stakeholders live.

If you want a finished machine to plug into, this is the wrong role. If you want to help build the machine, read on.

 

About the role

As our Founding SDR in London, you own outbound into UK enterprise accounts. You will prospect and open relationships with Finance and Procurement leaders (CFO, COO, Head of Shared Services, Process Excellence, AP) and generate qualified opportunities for our agentic AI platform automating Purchase-to-Pay and Order-to-Cash. Don’t expect inbounds to carry you from day one.

You are one of the first commercial hires on the ground in a new market. You prospect, you run the connect calls, and you help write the playbook the next UK hires will use. You report directly to the VP of Business Development for now, work day to day with the UK Account Executive as a tag-team, and lean on the DACH SDR team for what already works.

You will monitor the UK market with regards to procurement and finance processes, ERP transformation announcements and buying triggers, and turn what you learn into better targeting. We need you to flag what is not working early and bring it to the team, so we fix the approach fast instead of grinding on a broken one.

Once the UK team reaches critical mass and shows initial success, we hire a local team lead (internally or externally).

 

Tech stack

You will work with a sharp outbound stack: HubSpot as our CRM and source of truth, Clay for enrichment and signal-based prospecting, Claude for AI assisted tasks and research, and LinkMatch to keep LinkedIn and HubSpot in sync without manual logging. That said, the work has a strong outbound and calling focus. You will help decide what to add as the motion matures.

 

We're excited about you because

  • You have roughly 2 to 5 years of experience in a B2B SaaS SDR or BDR role, most of it outbound, and you have built or helped build an outbound motion rather than only working an established one.

  • You know the UK market and can navigate UK enterprise buyers, ideally with experience selling to Finance, Procurement, or Operations.

  • You can run a discovery call with a senior stakeholder: you hold the room, communicate clearly, adapt to a CFO or a Head of Procurement, and understand the buying center.

  • You are comfortable with ambiguity. No inbound, no case studies, no script on day one does not rattle you, it interests you. You see opportunity.

  • You enjoy problem-solving and have a natural curiosity that drives you to find creative solutions.

  • You are looking for a role that comes with key responsibility beyond the typical SDR scope.

  • You take ownership, ask for help when you are stuck, act on feedback, and pass on what you learn to the people who join after you.

Bonus points

  • You have been a founding or first SDR in a new market, or helped stand up a new territory.

  • You know the ERP domain, or have sold Finance, Procurement, or industrial software and are familiar with P2P/O2C processes.

  • You are familiar with HubSpot as a CRM and Clay.

  • You speak another European language.

 

What you'll get

  • London Office. This role is based in our London office, You will spend regular time with your DACH peers in our HQ in Zurich and are invited over for onboarding.

  • Onboarding built for a founding rep. There is onboarding material that trains you on our product, you get a buddy from the DACH SDR team and direct support from the VP Business Development.

  • Opportunities to grow. You're controlling your personal development and career trajectory in a rapidly growing, internationally expanding startup.

title: 3D Computer Vision Research Engineer - World Map
description:
About Niantic Spatial

AI has learned from almost everything online, but it still struggles with the physical world, where 99.5% of economic activity happens. It doesn’t know where things are, how spaces fit together, or what changes over time.

That’s one of the biggest unsolved problems in AI, and it’s the one we’re solving at Niantic Spatial. We build spatial AI models and services so people and machines can reason, learn and act safely in the physical world. We turn camera imagery, video, sensor data and archives into accurate, AI-readable representations of real places that robots can train in and machines can use to know exactly where they are.

In physical AI, mistakes have real consequences. That’s why we build AI grounded in measured reality, not guesswork, so the people and machines relying on it can trust it to get things right.

Our team built some of the world’s most widely used maps. Now we’re building something bigger: a living, measured record of the real world that machines can query, learn from and use to understand how places change over time. If you want to help AI understand the world we actually live in, come build with us.

About the Role

You'll help build the geometric foundation of the next-generation world map — joining our World Map Research Engineering team (Geospatial Alignment) as a Research Engineer or Senior Research Engineer. This is an end-to-end applied research role that spans from strong engineering and data-systems work to R&D in 3D deep learning, transformers, and foundation models. You'll develop new algorithms, produce the research data and evaluation assets needed to advance them, and engineer the resulting capabilities into dependable production systems.

The World Map team works with heterogeneous captures from phones and handheld devices, aerial imagery, LiDAR, and 360 cameras, as well as external geographic and elevation data. The central challenge is to harmonize these data sources, quantify uncertainty, and maintain consistency as the map evolves.

  • Establish a continuous discovery habit so research is a foundational reflex, and champion the user's perspective in every product decision.

 

Product & Experience Design

  • What our experts do by hand today is the spec for what the product must automate tomorrow. Your job is to watch that closely enough to design it.

title: Co-founder / Treuhänder/in – let's build the Treuhand of 2030
description:
Build the Treuhand of 2030.

Co-founder wanted: certified fiduciary (Treuhänder/in).

We believe that by 2030 at the latest, AI agents will handle most routine work in a Treuhand. That leaves fiduciaries with the work that needs judgment: reviewing, advising clients and signing off.

We are founding that Treuhand for Swiss startups and SMEs. AI agents prepare the work, and a qualified fiduciary signs off everything that goes to clients and authorities.

Underneath runs a finance stack built for agents, with clean data, a full audit trail and connections to the systems clients already use. Long term, we aim to run our clients' whole finance function on this stack, from bookkeeping to reporting, planning and investor/board updates.

Where we stand

The company is not founded yet. We are testing the problem in interviews with founders, CFOs and fiduciaries, three startups are interested in a paid pilot, and we have built a first prototype. You would join from day one and build the company with me. We will add a technical co-founder at a later stage.

Who you would work with

I'm Jonas Baer, two-time entrepreneur and fractional CFO for Swiss startups. As a Venturelab trainer and Innosuisse expert, I work closely with Swiss founders, the clients we want to serve. Before that I was CFO and director at a startup where we grew revenue to almost CHF 10M and the team to over 40. I studied Business Informatics at UZH and bridge finance and IT (linkedin.com/in/jonas-baer).

What you would do

  • Decide which workflows we automate first, where the AI acts alone and where a fiduciary signs

  • Teach the agents Swiss practice (MWST, AHV/BVG/UVG, booking rules) and test them on real documents

  • Serve the first pilot clients yourself

  • Build and lead the operations team as we scale

You have the final say on what gets booked, filed and signed.

What you bring

  • Treuhänder/in mit eidg. Fachausweis or dipl. Treuhandexperte/-in (or comparable)

  • 4+ years of experience with SMEs and startups

  • Hands-on with accounting systems such as Abacus, Bexio or Odoo (migration experience is a plus)

  • Daily user of AI tools

  • Founder mindset, comfortable deciding with incomplete information

  • Fluent in German and English

  • Based in or near Zürich

Your opportunity

This is your chance to design how a Treuhand works, with processes and tools you choose yourself. You join as co-founder with equity and start part-time. We agree on the details personally.

title: Flight Test Instrumentation & Data Engineer
description:
The Flight Test Instrumentation (FTI) & Data Engineer will be responsible for the end-to-end handling, quality assurance, accessibility, and long-term management of all flight data. The primary objective is to ensure that full-aircraft data, from the onboard sensors and DAQ systems to the final processing tools, is available to every engineering team through a reliable, efficient, and standardized workflow.

Tasks

Flight Test Instrumentation (FTI) & DAQ Pipeline

  • Manage the data pipeline from the physical sensor and Data Acquisition (DAQ) level for the full aircraft, ensuring seamless and accurate transmission into the telemetry and storage systems.
  • Maintain sensor configuration, calibration records, and metadata to guarantee the accurate translation of raw physical signals into usable engineering units.
  • Collaborate with hardware, software and integration teams to define sensor requirements, DAQ architectures, scaling, and telemetry bandwidth allocations.
  • Troubleshoot and resolve data anomalies at the DAQ and sensor level (e.g., signal noise, dropouts, faulty scaling) before they propagate into downstream databases.

Data Infrastructure & Accessibility

  • Maintain reliable extraction of flight data from InfluxDB.
  • Develop and maintain standardized local data structures for analysis, plotting, and visualization.
  • Optimize access to large flight datasets while minimizing CPU and memory usage.
  • Design and maintain an efficient local storage solution for processed flight data.
  • Support future improvements to the flight data architecture as storage requirements, sensor counts, and analysis needs continue to evolve.

Data Quality & Analysis Support

  • Maintain derived datasets to ensure common calculations and signals are shared consistently across teams.
  • Ensure strict timing synchronization and timestamp accuracy across all recorded data, from the sensor acquisition point to the database.
  • Monitor data quality, completeness, and integrity throughout the entire pipeline.
  • Provide fast data previews for rapid post-flight reviews.
  • Enable efficient access to high-frequency sensor data for detailed engineering investigations.
  • Support custom querying of processed datasets.

Requirements

Education & Experience

  • Bachelor’s or Master’s degree in Aerospace Engineering, Computer Science, Data Engineering, or a related technical field.
  • 3+ years of professional experience in test instrumentation, data acquisition (DAQ), or sensor-to-database time-series data engineering (aerospace, automotive, or racing/motorsports preferred).
  • Hands-on experience working directly with physical aircraft/vehicle sensor installations, DAQ hardware, and telemetry pipelines.

Technical & Domain Expertise

1. Hardware, Sensors & DAQ Architecture

  • Strong understanding of physical sensors (e.g., strain gauges, accelerometers, thermocouples, pressure transducers, RTDs, LVDTs, pitot-static tubes).
  • Demonstrated knowledge of signal conditioning, sampling rate selection, anti-aliasing filtering, scaling, and sensor calibration procedures.

2. Data Infrastructure & Software Development

  • Proficient in Python or MATLAB for data analysis, automated data processing, and visualization library development (e.g., Pandas, NumPy, SciPy).
  • Experience working with time-series databases, specifically InfluxDB (or similar engines), including writing efficient queries (Flux/InfluxQL) and data retrieval pipelines.
  • Solid foundation in data structures and memory/CPU optimization when handling high-memory high-frequency continuous time-series datasets.

3. Data Integrity & Signal Processing

  • Experience with timestamping and clock synchronization protocols across distributed DAQ hardware and storage nodes.
  • Knowledge of basic digital signal processing (DSP) concepts (filtering, FFT, spectral analysis, decimation/resampling).

Soft Skills & Work Style

  • Cross-functional communication: Ability to bridge the gap between hardware technicians, flight physics/aerodynamics engineers, and software teams.
  • Detail-oriented mindset: Uncompromising rigor regarding calibration metadata, unit conversions, and data accuracy.
  • Adaptability: Drive to continuously improve data infrastructure as aircraft sensor counts, test frequencies, and analytical needs expand.

Preferred / Bonus Qualifications

  • Knowledge of standard FAA / EASA flight test instrumentation requirements or military flight test standards (e.g. IRIG 106).
  • Familiarity with dashboarding tools (e.g., Grafana) for rapid post-flight previews and real-time telemetry display.
  • Experience with version control systems (Git) and CI/CD pipelines for internal engineering tool distribution.
  • Direct experience with DAQ systems and digital bus protocols (CAN bus, ARINC 429, MIL-STD-1553, Ethernet/UDP, PCM).
  • Familiarity with binary flight data formats (e.g., IRIG 106 Chapter 10/11, MDF/MF4, HDF5, Parquet, or custom binary loggers).
  • Experience with performing on-aircraft hardware troubleshooting (e.g., tracking down ground loops, signal noise, dropouts, or faulty scaling).

Monumental automatiseert de bouw met robotica en software. Onze missie is om de bouw software-defined en autonoom te maken – een toekomst waarin mooie gebouwen op maat in één dag verrijzen, met minimale inzet van handwerk.

We zijn een groeiend team van engineers, operators en technici, afkomstig van bedrijven als Palantir, Qualcomm, Dyson, Shopify, Tesla, Meta en Google DeepMind. We staan nog aan het begin van het opbouwen van dit bedrijf, en dit is je kans om buitenproportioneel veel impact te maken op een probleem dat écht uitmaakt. Vanaf dag één werk je samen met een ervaren foundingteam, met een Series B van $32M achter ons onder leiding van Khosla Ventures en Plural.

Monumental zit in het centrum van Amsterdam, in een prachtig pand met een volledig uitgeruste werkplaats en een eigen testvloer voor robots. We bouwen de hele stack in-house – hardware én software. We zijn uitdrukkelijk geen hybride of remote-first bedrijf: robots en muren bouw je niet vanaf je keukentafel, dus we werken vijf dagen per week op locatie.

Lees meer over waarom wij vinden dat je je tijd aan de bouw zou moeten besteden, en over onze visie en ons bedrijf. Misschien vind je ons YouTube-kanaal interessant, de film van Based in Europe over hoe we het Europese woningtekort aanpakken, of deze video van Andreas Klinger over hoe ons kantoor eruitziet.

Over de functie

De afgelopen jaren is Monumental gegroeid van een werkend product en de eerste proefprojecten naar bouwen op grote schaal. Inmiddels hebben we een vloot van meer dan 150 robots, die metselwerk hebben uitgevoerd voor meer dan 90 woningen, een school, een buurthuis, een hotel en meer dan 150 meter kanaalwand.

Elke maand nemen we meer bouwprojecten aan, intern noemen we die ‘deployments’. We werken met meer robots en meer mensen en breiden vanuit Nederland uit naar het Verenigd Koninkrijk en de VS.

Als Hub Lead zet je onze eerste vestiging buiten het hoofdkantoor op, in het noorden van Nederland. Je begint met ons grootste bouwproject tot nu toe. Naarmate er meer projecten bijkomen, bouw je het team en de operatie verder uit.

We zoeken mensen die breed inzetbaar zijn en een bouwproject willen leiden alsof het hun eigen bedrijf is. Achter elk project staat een Deployment Manager die van begin tot eind verantwoordelijk is. In de praktijk vervul je vijf rollen tegelijk: uitvoerder, operationeel manager, accountmanager, analist en projectmanager. Je maakt het bouwplan, voert het met je team als onderaannemer uit, onderhoudt het contact met de aannemer en zorgt dat we goed metselwerk op tijd opleveren. Dat doe je in de bouw, waar plannen voortdurend veranderen. Uiteindelijk leid je meerdere projecten tegelijk, waaronder complexe projecten waarbij veel op het spel staat.

De ene dag sta je bij zonsopgang op en ga je naar de bouwplaats. Je zaagt stenen, bewaakt de planning, stemt af met de hoofdaannemer en ziet je bouwplan steen voor steen werkelijkheid worden. De volgende dag zit je op onze vestiging, analyseer je de winst- en verliesrekening van je project en werk je aan systemen waarmee je bij het volgende project een betere marge haalt. Je bent verantwoordelijk voor de oplevering en geeft knelpunten die je op de bouwplaats tegenkomt door aan ons R&D-team.

Dit is intensief, praktisch werk op locatie, waar je veel voldoening uit kunt halen. Robots gaan kapot, het weer slaat om en de aannemer verandert het plan. Jij zorgt dat de bouw doorgaat.

Je krijgt veel vrijheid en verantwoordelijkheid. De rol past goed bij je als je eerder een bedrijf hebt opgericht, of als je een ondernemende functie zoekt waarin je veel invloed hebt op het resultaat.

Wat je gaat doen

  • De logistiek van een bouwproject plannen. Je bepaalt hoeveel en welke robots en mensen nodig zijn, stemt af met andere onderaannemers en maakt de dagelijkse planning. Tegelijk houd je het grotere geheel in het oog en begrijp je wat jouw keuzes betekenen voor de kosten en opbrengsten per project.

  • Op de bouwplaats het team aansturen, begeleiden en motiveren. Je onderhoudt het contact met hoofdaannemers en andere betrokkenen, vertegenwoordigt Monumental en legt uit wat we doen. Je schakelt net zo makkelijk met steigerbouwers als met de CEO’s van de grootste hoofdaannemers en onze engineers.

  • Operationele systemen opzetten waarmee elk project beter verloopt dan het vorige. Je ziet waar tijd en middelen verloren gaan, past processen aan en verbetert de marge.

  • Samenwerken met bestaande klanten en zorgen dat daar nieuwe bouwprojecten uit voortkomen. In de toekomst doe je dat ook voor aanverwante productlijnen buiten het metselwerk.

  • Verantwoordelijkheid nemen voor de winst- en verliesrekening van je project en voorstellen doen om de kosten en opbrengsten per project steeds verder te verbeteren.

  • Helpen bij het werven en interviewen van nieuwe robotoperators en deployment operators.

Wat we zoeken

  • Minimaal drie jaar ervaring startupervaring, als operator, manager, of founder.

  • Nederlands als moedertaal. De bouwsector is sterk lokaal georganiseerd, dus dit is een vereiste voor de functie.

  • Je communiceert helder en makkelijk met mensen met uiteenlopende achtergronden.

  • Je bent bereid om letterlijk je handen vuil te maken om het werk gedaan te krijgen.

  • Je komt snel in actie, zet door en krijgt dingen voor elkaar. In deze functie draait het vooral om uitvoeren.

  • Je kunt goed omgaan met hoge werkdruk. Op bouwplaatsen gaat regelmatig iets mis en staat er veel op het spel. Daar komt bij dat we nieuwe technologie inzetten waarvan we nog niet alle mogelijke storingen kennen.

  • Je denkt scherp en leert graag. Welke achtergrond je ook hebt, je zult in deze rol veel en snel moeten leren. Het werk kan elke drie tot zes maanden als een nieuwe baan voelen. Je leert veel over de bouw, robotica en werken in een snelgroeiend technologiebedrijf.

  • Je hebt ervaring met het aansturen van een klein team en weet hoe je mensen begeleidt en motiveert.

  • Je bent operationeel en analytisch sterk. Je kunt een helder operationeel plan uitwerken in een spreadsheet, een winst- en verliesrekening presenteren en verschillende scenario’s doorrekenen, inclusief de factoren die het resultaat bepalen. Je bent een sterke projectmanager.

Waarom Monumental?

Bij Monumental werken betekent vooroplopen in een beweging die de bouwsector wezenlijk wil veranderen. Jouw werk heeft hier niet alleen impact op het bedrijf, maar op de toekomst van hoe we bouwen. Als je gedreven wordt door innovatie, graag complexe uitdagingen aanpakt en klaar bent om echt verschil te maken, horen we graag van je.

title: Director, Expanded Access Program Operations
description:
About myTomorrows 

myTomorrows is a global health tech company dedicated to breaking down barriers for patients seeking treatment options.   

We strive to enable earlier and better treatment access by bridging the gap between those searching for possible options, and the companies who develop them. We work closely with patients, healthcare professionals, trial sites, patient advocacy groups, and BioPharma – connecting key stakeholders in the drug development ecosystem.   

We’ve developed a cutting-edge AI-powered technology platform that simplifies and streamlines access to drugs in development. To support our users and clients, we have a range of industry-expert specialized teams ready to help. Our services include clinical trial patient recruitment, Expanded Access Program management and Real-World Data collection.   

With a global footprint spanning 134 countries, to date we’ve supported over 17,000 patients, 3,000 physicians and 350 sites, earning the trust of 60+ BioPharma companies. In October 2025, we closed a €25M investment with Avego Healthcare Capital to fuel our global ambitions and scale the business.  

Join us in shaping the future of treatment access - making tomorrow’s therapies accessible for people who need them today. 

The opportunity: Director of EAP Operations (Expanded Access Programs and Site Management)

This is a high‑impact leadership role at the heart of how myTomorrows delivers Expanded Access Programs (EAPs) globally—where operational excellence meets commercial acumen.

As Director of EAP Operations, you’ll own the end‑to‑end operational delivery of our EAP portfolio, integrating Program Management and Site Management into one scalable, outcome‑driven model. Beyond ensuring quality, compliance, speed, and resilience, you’ll be expected to think like an entrepreneur: spotting opportunities, optimising processes, and driving commercially sound decisions that enable sustainable growth.

You’ll be a core member of the Operations Leadership Team and report directly to our COO (Vanessa says hi). This role is perfect for someone who thrives on complexity, builds high‑performing teams, and raises the operational bar—while balancing patient‑first decision‑making with a strong commercial mindset.

Geographic Requirement: This role is open to candidates in The Netherlands, United Kingdom, Canada and USA. For candidates in North America, to ensure seamless collaboration with our teams, applicants must reside within the EST or CST time zones.

What you'll do in this role:

  • Own the end-to-end operating model for EAP Program + Site Management, ensuring scalable and compliant delivery

  • Translate strategy and portfolio forecasts into capacity planning, org design and hiring priorities

  • Build resilient coverage and escalation models across the portfolio (no single points of failure)

  • Lead the EAP Program Management team to deliver consistent execution across clients and geographies

  • Lead the EAP Site Management team to ensure strong site engagement, workload balance and service performance

  • Drive standardisation and continuous improvement across ways of working, tooling and operational excellence

  • Set and run a strong governance rhythm: KPIs, performance reviews, risk management and quality oversight

  • Act as senior escalation point for complex delivery, regulatory and stakeholder challenges

  • Grow a bar-raising leadership bench through coaching, performance management and succession planning

  • Partner with Finance, People and Operations on budgeting, workforce planning and scale-up decisions

What you bring to the table:

  • You have 8–10+ years experience leading and managing expanded access programs.

  • Experience in a market access setting and with multi-country reimbursement strategies is a plus.

  • You understand the EAP business, and have a strong and proven commercial and client service mindset.

  • You have proven experience building and leading high performance teams.

  • You know how to lead managers and scale operational teams in complex settings

  • You have an exceptionally strong understanding of compliance, regulatory frameworks and operational requirements in the context of Expanded Access Programs

  • You have a track record of operational excellence: scaling delivery, managing risk, and raising performance standards

  • You are a strategic thinker with strong execution focus — you simplify complexity and drive outcomes

  • You are a confident stakeholder manager who can align senior leaders and external partners

  • You hold a high bar for quality and accountability, with calm leadership under pressure

What success in the first 6 months looks like:

  • Have full grip on the EAP portfolio and delivery realities — and you can clearly articulate the biggest operational opportunities and risks (and have recommendations on how to address them)

  • Create clarity across Program & Site Management: ownership, workflows, escalation paths, and what “great” looks like

  • Have strengthened the operating model to improve consistency, speed and resilience across the portfolio

  • Have managed to deliver on the expected ramp-up of the EAP business both in terms of patients served, and revenue generated.

  • Have implemented a clear KPI rhythm (quality, timelines, compliance, service levels) with transparent performance reporting

  • Have improved capacity planning and coverage, educing single points of failure and enabling predictable delivery

  • Have made at least 1–2 concrete operational improvements (process / tooling / standardisation) that measurably improve delivery outcomes

  • Are seen as a trusted Operations Leadership Team member who raises the bar and builds momentum.

Equal opportunities

myTomorrows is an Equal Opportunity Employer and, beyond upholding discrimination-free practices, we are committed to cultivating a workplace where difference and diversity are protected and celebrated. The best work comes from our best selves, and we go to great lengths in supporting our team members to be just that.

Former Auditor - Senior Customer Success Manager

As a Senior Customer Success Manager (+Audit Background) at DataSnipper, you own the success of a portfolio of accounts - and you bring something additional to the role: direct experience in audit. You understand how audit teams work, what drives their priorities, and how to connect DataSnipper to the workflows that matter most inside a firm.

You are a reliable, independent operator who applies established CS frameworks and uses your audit knowledge to accelerate adoption, build credibility with audit stakeholders, and design enablement that non-audit CSMs cannot replicate. You manage onboarding, QBRs, health monitoring, and renewals with predictability and follow-through and you do it in a language audit professionals trust.

You may still be developing the full breadth of CS scope, but your audit domain credibility opens doors and unlocks conversations that are otherwise harder to access at this level.

 

About DataSnipper

Audit and finance are still massively manual and we are changing that. DataSnipper is a $1B, bootstrapped unicorn with 600,000+ users across 180+ countries, already embedded in the daily workflows of top audit and accounting firms.

Now, we are taking things further with our Excel Agent, bringing AI directly into where the work actually happens. Unlike generic AI tools, we do not sit on the sidelines. Our AI operates inside Excel, with access to real documents and audit evidence, meaning it does not just generate answers, it does the work, with full traceability.

We are not just applying AI, we are redefining how audit gets done. If you want to build something category-defining at scale, this is the place.

  • Act as a Credible Audit Advisor: Serve as a trusted partner to Audit Managers, Senior Auditors, and engagement team leads. title: Team Lead, Data Engineering
description:
We are looking for a Data Engineering Team Lead to lead the Data Platform team at DataSnipper.

Every decision DataSnipper makes about its products runs through the data platform: which features land, which customers are getting value, what we bill for, what we fix next, and which AI capabilities add the most value. You will lead a team of two data engineers who own the systems that make that possible. That means how usage events get captured across a growing set of products, how they become trustworthy models in Snowflake, and how Customer Success, Product and GTM get to answers without waiting on us.

This is a player-coach role in a small, high-ownership team. You are responsible for the people, the roadmap and the technical direction, and you stay hands-on enough to ship alongside the team and make architectural calls credibly. At DataSnipper, Team Lead is our entry point into engineering management: the same people, delivery and product responsibilities as an Engineering Manager, on a smaller team.

We are a handful of people serving the whole company, so your judgment about what not to build matters as much as what the team ships.

About DataSnipper

DataSnipper is the driving force behind an intelligent automation platform that’s transforming the world of audit and finance.

Founded in 2017, DataSnipper has skyrocketed and is now OFFICIALLY the fastest-growing software company in the Netherlands according to Deloitte Fast50 and recently achieved Unicorn status in our latest funding round. With over 400.000 users in 125+ countries and a second base in the heart of New York City, DataSnipper is shaking things up. And we’re not stopping there. At DataSnipper, we’re always on the lookout for innovators who think outside of the box. New ideas aren’t just welcomed at DataSnipper–they’re essential.

What your team owns

The Data Platform team works across three areas:

  • Data Platform: reliable, scalable infrastructure that gets the right data to the right place

  • Internal Analytics: a self-service platform so every team can be data-informed without a ticket

  • Customer-facing Analytics: the dashboards and exports customers use to see the value they get from DataSnipper

Concretely, you would be walking into billions of usage events flowing from our Excel Add-in, web apps and product backends through Azure Event Hubs into Snowflake; a dbt estate built on medallion principles and managed in dbt Cloud; Terraform-managed Snowflake and Azure infrastructure; and a set of product teams shipping AI agents faster than we can instrument them.

You will also find real, named open problems rather than a tidy platform: event capture mid-consolidation, multiple methods of user attribution, and a data quality layer that is designed but not yet built. We would rather tell you that up front.

What you will do

Lead the team

  • Lead a team of two data engineers through outcomes, not tasks: set clear goals with the team and trust them to figure out how

  • Make the team measurably better: raise the engineering bar, grow each engineer into bigger problems, and address performance issues directly when they arise

  • Run regular 1:1s, give clear and timely feedback, and own each engineer's goals and development

  • Foster a culture of experimentation, learning, documentation and operational excellence

  • Take part in hiring and help shape the team's scope as it evolves

Own direction and delivery

  • Partner closely with Product, Engineering, Customer Success and GTM to shape the team's roadmap, turning vague data requests into scoped, well-defined work

  • Make the trade-offs a small team serving the whole company needs: what to build, what to defer, and when a request shouldn't become a pipeline

  • Set the technical direction and make the architectural calls that shape the team's systems

  • Keep Snowflake performance and cost, tech debt, dependencies and compliance obligations (audit logging, vulnerability remediation, Vanta evidence) visible and under control

  • Be the person other engineering teams come to when they need to instrument something new

Stay hands-on in the data platform

  • Contribute to the event ingestion architecture end to end: Azure Event Hubs, Snowpipe, Fivetran, and our shared Python/TypeScript event client libraries

  • Build and review dbt transformation pipelines that stay reliable as volume, source count and model complexity grow

  • Define and enforce event contracts and schemas so product teams can instrument new features without silent breakage downstream

  • Evolve the core data models (event, user, license, company) and integrate new sources such as product backends, MongoDB, HubSpot and billing

  • Guide reverse ETL and activation work that pushes modeled data back into HubSpot, MongoDB, Postgres and GTM reporting

What you bring

Leadership

  • At least 1 year leading engineers as a team lead or engineering manager: 1:1s, feedback, goal setting, performance, and development

  • An empowerment style of leadership: you lead through outcomes and trust, not by assigning tasks

  • Early evidence of growing engineers and raising a team's bar, and the willingness to address performance issues directly

  • Strong product aptitude: you can challenge the framing of a request, translate stakeholder needs into technical solutions, and make roadmap trade-offs


Data engineering

  • 7+ years in data engineering or a closely related backend/platform role, with a track record of owning a data platform area end to end

  • Deep SQL and strong Python, including query optimization and performance tuning on a cloud warehouse

  • Production experience with a cloud data warehouse (we use Snowflake) and a modern transformation framework (we use dbt)

  • Experience with event-driven / streaming ingestion and its failure modes: schema drift, duplication, late data, backfills

  • Experience on a cloud platform at the infrastructure level (we're on Azure; AWS/GCP transfers fine)

  • Solid data modeling fundamentals and the ability to defend a modeling decision to both engineers and business stakeholders

  • Experience operating data systems in production with a focus on reliability, observability and maintainability


How you work

  • Excellent communication in English and genuine comfort working directly with non-technical stakeholders

  • Bias to action, a strong sense of ownership, and the judgment to prioritize when demand exceeds capacity

Preferred qualifications

  • Experience in a startup or scale-up, ideally as an early member of a data team

  • Experience hiring engineers or helping a team expand its scope

  • Experience with product analytics tooling (Mixpanel, RudderStack) and warehouse-native BI (Netspring/Optimizely Analytics, Omni, Embeddable, or similar)

  • Experience building data products for AI or agent consumption: semantic layers, metrics layers, MCP servers, or governed self-service access

  • Experience with Terraform, Docker and data governance at scale

  • Reverse ETL experience and familiarity with CRM data models (HubSpot, Salesforce) or customer success platforms


What we offer

  • Being part of one of the fastest-growing scale-ups in the Netherlands

  • Make an impact by disrupting the audit industry with us

  • A step into engineering management, with Engineering Manager scope on a small team

  • 28 vacation days

  • Excellent salary

  • Pension plan

  • Stock participation plan

  • Hybrid work (Amsterdam-based)

  • International team and environment

title: Senior Regulatory Affairs Specialist
description:
The Practical Detail
Location: Wageningen
Working model: Hybrid

Why this role matters
You will lead regulatory compliance across Europe, ensuring our innovative products meet and exceed all requirements.
This role is crucial for guiding product development and marketing strategies within Flora Food Group, helping us deliver Culinary Essentials for Better Food.
You will influence business-critical decisions by translating complex regulations into clear guidance, balancing compliance with creativity and speed to market.
Your work supports our purpose by enabling safe, compliant, and innovative food solutions that reach kitchens across Europe.

What you'll do

  • Guide Product Developers and Technical Project Leaders from project inception to launch, ensuring regulatory compliance for innovative products and claims.
  • Shape and implement Flora Food Group's marketing claims strategy and risk management plans.
  • Anticipate, identify, and manage regulatory changes across Europe, driving their implementation within the business.
  • Train and support cross-functional teams including R&D, Marketing, and Sales on regulatory frameworks such as product and labelling compliance, nutrition and health claims, and regulatory processes.
  • Liaise with Legal, Quality, Corporate Affairs, and Marketing teams to address regulatory and compliance questions from authorities and customers.

Performance
You will own regulatory leadership across Europe, ensuring compliance that enables innovation and market success. You will translate regulatory requirements into clear, pragmatic guidance for the business, balancing compliance, innovation, creativity, and speed to market, while driving continuous improvement of regulatory processes, tools, and ways of working.
Success will be measured through effective business partnering, timely project support, compliant product delivery, and continuous improvement initiatives.

Care
You will report to the Regulatory Affairs Manager for Developed Markets (Europe) and work closely with diverse teams across R&D, Marketing, Legal, Quality, and Corporate Affairs.
Your role demands responsible leadership, balancing regulatory compliance with business needs to build sustainable, long-term solutions.
You will foster collaboration and accountability, ensuring Flora Food Group's products meet the highest standards for consumers and communities.

Passion
As a food lover and regulatory expert, you bring curiosity and rigor to navigating complex food regulations.
You understand the importance of taste, nutrition, functionality, and reliability in every product we develop.
Your passion for food innovation drives you to support creative solutions that meet regulatory demands without compromising quality or consumer trust.

About you
You bring strong experience in European food regulations within an FMCG environment, with a proven ability to influence and guide cross-functional teams.
You have a Master's Degree or higher in Food Technology, Quality, Chemistry, or a related field, combined with practical experience in regulatory affairs.
You are proactive, able to manage time-sensitive priorities, and skilled at translating complex regulatory requirements into clear, pragmatic guidance.
Fluency in English is essential, and additional languages are a plus.
You are genuinely interested in food culture and curious about how consumer behaviour and future food trends shape innovation.
You understand that strong brands are built by anticipating what's next in taste, nutrition and functionality, and by translating insight into meaningful consumer experiences.

Where this could lead to
This role typically leads to progression into the Regulatory Affairs Manager position, with opportunities to expand into Nutrition, Corporate Affairs, or Communications depending on your background and aspirations. Growth is supported by increasing responsibility for regulatory strategy and cross-functional leadership within Flora Food Group.

At Zattoo, you’re always on firm ground with real freedom to explore. You’ll have the support and opportunity you need to go far, while you’re helping us create a sustainable and entertainment-filled future for all.

title: Member of Scientific Staff, Cell Culture and Functional Assays
description:
LOCATION: King's Cross, London · PATTERN: Lab-based, full-time

The opportunity

We're a stealth startup in AI and bio, building infrastructure for data generation. The team is small and elite, the problems are hard, and the foundations are being laid right now. You'd help write them from the first line, with real ownership and a direct line to the founders.

This role covers the cell side of our protein characterisation work. You would keep the cell lines healthy and run the assays that show how a designed protein behaves on a living cell, week after week, to the same standard.

About us

AI for biology has a data problem. The data that matters most doesn't exist yet, so we're building the infrastructure to produce it, with quality and traceability built in from day one.

We're in stealth and heads-down on execution. We'll share more about what we're building once you've spoken with the team.

The role

You will run cell culture and the cell-based assays for our protein characterisation work. That means the mammalian lines the assays depend on, from thaw through routine passage to a banked and documented stock, and the weekly rhythm of seeding, treating, reading and reporting plates.

Most of it runs in 384-well plates with imaging-based or flow cytometry readouts. You will run those assays as designed, with the controls and replicates that make a curve defensible, and you will be the person who notices when a plate, a line or a reagent lot has started to drift.

Assay design and the shape of the cascade sit with the scientist who leads this work today, so you are not being asked to invent the panel. You are being asked to make it run the same way every week, to record what you did in a form the rest of the system can read, and to tighten the protocols as they settle, including moving them towards the plate formats our automation will take on.

Your first 90 days

FIRST 30 DAYS

◆ Take over routine culture and banking for the protein cell lines, working to the protocols we already run.

◆ Learn the panel end to end by running each assay alongside the scientist who owns it.

DAYS 30 TO 60

◆ Run at least one assay in the panel independently, including its controls and acceptance criteria.

◆ Revise one culture or assay protocol so that someone else could follow it without asking you.

DAYS 60 TO 90

◆ Hold the weekly assay schedule on your own and return results on the agreed turnaround.

◆ Bring one protocol to a tighter precision bar, or into a plate format ready for automation.

Who you are

You are a hands-on cell biologist who takes assay variability personally. You have run the same assay often enough to tell a real effect from a bad plate, and you would rather find the cause than repeat the run.

The week has a rhythm in this job: cells to feed, plates to seed, runs to finish, numbers to return. You are happy with that, you keep records someone else can pick up, and you say early when something looks wrong rather than at the end of the week.

We do not hire people into boxes. The team is small, and early hires here end up owning work beyond the job they joined for. Nobody arrives with every part of this role. If you are strong in most of it and quick to learn the rest, we want to hear from you.

MUST HAVE

◆ Strong hands-on mammalian cell culture: adherent and suspension lines, aseptic technique, and thawing, passaging and banking to a high and consistent standard.

◆ Experience running cell-based assays end to end, including relevant controls, replicates and dose-response curves behind a reported number.

◆ Comfort with plate-based work and the arithmetic that goes with it, such as dilution series, plate maps and normalisation.

◆ Careful, traceable record-keeping that someone else can follow without asking you.

◆ A PhD in cell biology, pharmacology, immunology or a related field, or an MSc and two to three years of relevant lab experience.

NICE TO HAVE

◆ Reporter cell line bioassays for binding or blockade.

◆ Receptor internalisation, lysosomal trafficking or cytotoxicity assays.

◆ High-content or fluorescence imaging, and the image analysis behind it.

◆ 384-well formats, liquid handlers or other plate-based automation.

◆ Flow cytometry, for example for surface receptor quantification.

Why this is unusual

Most cell-based assay roles sit inside a discovery project. You build an assay, you answer a question with it, and the assay goes quiet. This one is closer to running an instrument. The same assays run every week against a stream of new molecules, and the number that comes out is the product.

That changes what good looks like. Precision matters more than novelty, a protocol is only finished when someone else can run it and get your answer, and every passage, plate and reagent lot is captured as structured data, because a result is only as trustworthy as the cells behind it.

Some people find that energising; some find it outside their lane. Worth knowing in advance which one you are.

How we work

This is a lab-based role at our site in King's Cross, London. The cells are in the lab, so most of your week will be too, with room for writing and analysis away from the bench. The wider team is distributed and travels, so you will work with people who are not always in the building.

We work in the open. Decisions are written down, work happens centrally rather than scattered across tools, and the week opens with a session the whole company attends. There is a quarterly offsite. Each person owns their area and makes the call inside it, and we will expect that of you early rather than late.

UK benefits are 30 days of annual leave plus public holidays, a pension with a 10% employer contribution, and top-tier Bupa private health cover. More is added as the team grows.

The team you will join

You will join the protein characterisation team and report to its lead. Day to day you will work with the scientist who designs the assay cascade, with the protein production and molecular characterisation scientists upstream of you, with the functional genomics team who share the cell culture suite, and with the engineers building the software and automation the lab runs on.

We are a small, elite team, and this is the first seat given entirely to the cell-based side of the work.

Our process

Our process has four stages. A short screening call about the role and the practicalities. A behavioural interview about how you work, run from the same template for every candidate, before anything technical. A technical stage with the protein characterisation team, built around real work rather than a puzzle, including time with us in person at the lab. Then references, aimed at whatever we still want to understand.

If you are not sure whether you match every line above, apply anyway. We would rather read it and decide.

We are an equal opportunity employer. We make hiring decisions on merit, scope-fit, and the strength of the working relationship we expect to build with each hire. Applications welcome from candidates of any background.

Understanding is non-negotiable

Understanding leads to believing. Believing leads to winning.

About Duvo

Before Duvo, our founders built and ran a $2 billion retailer. They saw how much critical work still depended on spreadsheets, inboxes, supplier portals and the memory of experienced operators. The real process rarely lived in one system. People held the last mile together.

Duvo is building the Enterprise Execution OS: the shared layer that understands how work really runs, carries it across existing systems and measures the business result.

Our agents do the work, not just suggest the next step. They gather evidence, make decisions within agreed rules, route exceptions to the right person and update the source system. People keep control wherever judgment or approval is needed. Every action leaves an audit trail.

We start with one recurring process and a clear outcome. Every solution carries a contracted 5x ROI guarantee.

The role

As a Junior Transformation Strategist, you are the insight and output engine beside our Transformation Strategists on our largest accounts.

On bigger engagements we need more than technical delivery. We need someone who can take a messy process, find the critical question, get to a clear insight fast, and put it into materials a customer team will act on. Today that work often lands on Forward Deployed Engineers. That is the wrong use of a scarce technical resource. This role exists so that insight work has a dedicated owner.

You will work alongside Transformation Strategists (who own day-to-day account presence and workstream direction) and Forward Deployed Engineers (who own the technical solution). You do not own the executive relationship or the commercial outcome. You own the speed and quality of the analytical and written work that makes those conversations possible.

This is a fungible problem-solving role. You will be thrown at different accounts and different problem types (category, supply chain, finance ops, inventory, commercial) and expected to produce. Ideal for someone currently ~2–4 years into a client-facing career as an Associate, Senior Associate, or Consultant at McKinsey or BCG who wants concentrated ownership, not another staffing cycle.

We want to hire two people into this role quickly.

What you will do

1. Get to the insight

  • Dive into how work actually happens: interviews, extracts, handoffs, exceptions and the workarounds people use to keep things running.

  • Build a fact base that shows where cost, cash, service, cycle time or control is being lost.

  • Form a hypothesis early, name what would kill it, and pressure-test it with the Transformation Strategist before you polish anything.

  • Structure unfamiliar problems without waiting for a perfect brief. Frame the selection equation (what matters, what does not) so the team and the customer can decide.

2. Deliver output that moves a decision

  • Turn analysis into decision-ready slides, one-pagers and memos that make the important choice obvious.

  • Be exact about baselines, assumptions and evidence. Do not use polish to hide uncertainty.

  • Work fast: same-day or next-day turnarounds on defined asks are the norm, not the exception.

  • Produce materials a Transformation Strategist can take into a working session or steerco with minimal rewrite.

3. Be fungible surge capacity on big accounts

  • Plug into multiple live enterprise accounts as extra hands where the Transformation Strategist needs analytical depth.

  • Jump between problem types without needing a long ramp each time.

  • Keep a clean trail of actions, open questions and evidence so work can be handed between you, the Transformation Strategist and the FDE without loss.

  • Surface blockers early; do not sit on ambiguity hoping it resolves.

4. Build the evidence for impact

  • Help lock baseline, target and measurement window before implementation.

  • Quantify results in language a CFO would trust (revenue, margin, cost, working capital, cycle time, control), not activity counts or sentiment.

  • Investigate misses as carefully as wins, and turn both into clear evidence packs the Transformation Strategist can use upstairs.

5. Stay close to the customer team (working level)

  • Own relationships with operators and mid-level owners who live the process day to day.

  • Prepare working sessions, capture decisions and follow commitments through.

  • Know when a question needs a senior call and escalate early rather than bluffing.

You will not own commercial negotiations, board-level relationships or technical build. You will own the craft and pace of the insight work that makes those outcomes possible.

Skills and capabilities we will assess

These are explicit. We will hire against them.

  • Structured problem solving. Hypothesis-driven. You can take an unfamiliar operation apart, find the critical question, write a kill criterion, and give a clear recommendation without hiding behind a framework.

  • Analytical speed and numeracy. Comfortable with messy data and incomplete information. You build analyses that are concise, correct and decision-ready under time pressure.

  • Written and slide craft. Your decks and memos are tight. First page says the answer. Evidence follows. A partner or Transformation Strategist can use your output with light edit, not a rewrite.

  • Insight generation. You do not stop at describing the process. You find where value is lost and what to change first.

  • Fungibility. You can be dropped onto a new account or a new problem type and produce within days, not weeks.

  • Delivery bias. You stay after the framing is done. You follow actions through. You notice what is not working and help fix it.

  • Customer judgment at working level. You listen well, ask a direct question and communicate clearly with operators and managers. You know when to escalate.

  • AI-native personal workflow. You use AI seriously to accelerate research, analysis and drafting, and you remain responsible for the quality of what goes in front of a customer.

  • Early-stage working style. You move without perfect instructions, write in plain English and surface bad news early.

Who we are looking for

  • Currently an Associate, Senior Associate or Consultant (or equivalent) at McKinsey or BCG, typically ~2–4 years of core, client-facing consulting experience. Bain and other top strategy firms can fit if the craft is the same.

  • A track record of producing high-quality analyses and slides that partners and clients actually used to decide.

  • Evidence you can work quickly without sacrificing rigor.

  • Comfort operating as surge capacity across problems rather than owning a single long study end to end alone.

Helpful but not required: retail, CPG, supply chain, logistics, inventory or finance operations exposure; prior startup or early-stage experience.

What good looks like after 12 months

  • Transformation Strategists on our largest accounts treat you as the person they call when they need a sharp fact base, a clean deck or a second pair of eyes on an insight, within hours not days.

  • You have supported multiple accounts and problem types without losing quality.

  • At least one measured process change carries analysis and evidence you built.

  • Your templates, diagnostics and slide patterns are reused by the next Junior Transformation Strategist.

  • FDEs on those accounts spend their time on technical delivery, not insight decks.

This role is not for you if

  • You want to own the C-level relationship, commercial negotiation or full transformation roadmap from day one. That is the Transformation Strategist / Senior path.

  • You only enjoy the framing phase and lose interest once the work becomes detailed.

  • You need perfectly clean data, a large analyst team or complete instructions before you can make progress.

  • You see slides as the final product rather than a tool to help a customer decide and act.

  • You want to build automations or live in the technical weeds. That is the Forward Deployed Engineer role.

  • You want a narrow, single-account BA role with little variety or visible accountability.

Why leave McKinsey or BCG for this

  • Your insight work lands in live enterprise operations with a contracted 5x ROI, not in a forgotten sharepoint.

  • You sit beside Transformation Strategists and FDEs on real accounts, so you see recommendation through to adoption.

  • You get concentrated ownership of analytical craft instead of being staffed for utilization.

  • Direct access to founders, customers and decisions in a small team.

  • Stay close to the customer. Know their real day better than the process document.

This role is UK-based. You will need to be living in the UK, or relocating there before you start, and able to travel to client sites from there. Expect regular travel and periods on site with customers for several days in a week when projects are live.

What we offer

  • Competitive compensation and meaningful equity, with flexibility in the balance between cash and ownership.

  • Direct access to founders, customers and decisions.

  • The budget and autonomy to use the best AI tools available.

We respect your time and move fast:

  1. Screening call.

  2. Hiring manager interview. Fit on problem-solving craft, pace and whether this is the right altitude for you.

  3. Case study panel. A live enterprise problem that tests structure, numbers, prioritisation and clear communication (including slide / written output).
