Senior Test Automation Engineer
Senior RFP & Bid Manager, EMEA
Engineering Manager – Robot Intelligence
description:
About the Role at RobCo

RobCo is building the category of Autonomous Industrial Robotics and we're doing it fast. We believe that automating the ordinary frees humans to do the extraordinary, and we're building the end-to-end robotics infrastructure to make that possible - hardware, software, and AI in one stack that just works.

 

We are now looking for an ambitious Engineering Manager - Robot Intelligence (m/f/d) to help us establish RobCo as a leading provider of autonomous automation solutions.

In this key role, you will lead the “brain” of our autonomous robots - the physical AI harness that works with different models and skills. Managing a full-stack team of software and machine learning engineers, you will balance applied research with business value delivery on a daily basis.

Your mission is to translate the latest advancements in physical AI foundation models and complex robotic functionality into a stable, scalable product that thrives in real-world factory environments.

Your Responsibilities:

  • Drive Engineering Excellence: Set rigorous standards for code quality, automated testing, and CI/CD pipelines to ensure 24/7 reliability of our robots.

  • Lead Senior Talent: Act as a people-first leader for a team of Senior and Staff engineers, fostering a culture of high ownership and steady delivery.

  • Bridge Software and Hardware: Oversee the lifecycle of products spanning from ML training, AI inference to Linux-based industrial interfaces.

  • Balance Research and Delivery: Establish a strong applied research and experimentation culture, and build a process where the results directly contribute to delivery and practical outcomes.

  • Management Framework: Work with real-time metrics and steer the team to continuously improve productivity, predictability and quality of what we ship.

  • Operational Governance: Manage technical debt and architectural health to ensure long-term system stability as we scale.

  • Strategic Alignment: Partner with Product Management to transform customer needs into concrete technical requirements and actionable sprints.

  • Cross-Team Leadership: Mentor junior EMs and help evolve company-wide engineering best practices and software-first principles.

We are looking for someone who has:

  • Completed a university degree in Computer Science, Robotics, Engineering, Data Science or a related field.

  • 3+ years of experience leading high-performing teams in complex technical environments like robotics or industrial IoT.

  • Deep experience with AI and machine learning, including dataset curation, model training and optimization techniques and hands on experience building agentic harnesses.

  • Proven track record of driving an AI-first engineering culture and implementing agentic workflows that measurably accelerate team velocity and system efficiency.

  • Expert knowledge in modern SDLC practices, with a track record of improving deployment frequency and system stability.

  • Culture-aligned mindset characterized by hardware empathy, a passion for software-defined hardware, and a strong culture of high ownership.

  • Strong experience with full-stack software development, robotics engineering is a big plus.

  • Very good English skills with the ability to navigate complex architectural discussions with Staff engineers while clearly communicating risks to stakeholders.

Why join RobCo?

  • Develop modular, software-defined robotics solutions with us that set new standards in automation.

  • Help us build robots equipped with state-of-the-art AI that perceive their environment, analyze data, and make intelligent decisions in real time.

  • As part of a very dynamic and fast-growing scale-up, you will take on responsibility from day one, drive your own projects, and see the direct impact of your work.

  • Flat hierarchies, open communication, and regular 360° feedback enable fast decisions and support your professional and personal development.

  • Wellpass membership (7,200+ studios across Germany), regular team events, and a team that takes both the work and the culture seriously.

  • Flexible working hours, a modern office, and - depending on the role - the option to work from home.

  • Regular team events - from relaxed beer & pizza nights on the rooftop terrace to shared experiences on ski trips or at Oktoberfest.

About RobCo

Founded in Munich in 2020, RobCo leads the transition toward fully Autonomous Industrial Robotics. Our mission is to deploy RobCo in every factory - solving the industrial labor shortage through end-to-end robotics that just works. Powered by Physical AI, our solutions combine a scalable modular hardware architecture with intelligent software that adapts to your use case, improves over time, and requires zero upfront investment through our Robotics-as-a-Service (RaaS) model.

We solve our customers' most pressing pain points - labor shortage, cost pressure, workplace safety, and national reshoring - across the full spectrum of Autonomous Industrial Robotics. With $160M raised from investors including Lightspeed, Lingotto Innovation, and Sequoia, 200+ people globally, and 2.5M+ operating hours in the field, we are deploying robots in factories across Europe and the United States - with our US operations headquartered in Austin, TX, and our RobCo Bay Area Demo Lab in San Francisco.

Don’t meet every single requirement? If you’re excited about this role but your past experience doesn’t align perfectly with every qualification in the job description, we encourage you to apply anyway. You may be just the right candidate for this or other roles.

At RobCo, applicants are selected regardless of ethnic origin, religion, gender, age, disability, or sexual orientation. All decisions throughout the recruitment process are based solely on applicants’ qualifications, skills, knowledge, and experience, as well as relevant business requirements.

Logistics? Maybe not what you dreamed of as a kid. But building a fast-growing international SaaS scale-up that's transforming how some of the world's largest industrial companies operate? That's a different story.

Peripass is a tech company at heart. We build software that digitises and automates complex logistics environments for companies like Bridgestone, Kellanova/Kellogg’s and ArcelorMittal.   • Own the full sales cycle: You will be responsible for selling our SaaS solution and independently managing qualified sales opportunities from initial engagement through signed contract. This includes identifying and qualifying prospects, conducting discovery conversations, developing business cases, managing stakeholders, negotiating and closing deals.

  • Build our presence in the UK: Identify target accounts and create new business opportunities through strategic outbound prospecting and personalised outreach across relevant industries. Work closely with our BDR team to open conversations with new prospects and build awareness of Peripass in the UK market.

  • Front-row seat to scale-up growth: Be part of the next growth phase of Peripass in the UK and have a direct impact on building our market presence.

  • Backed by a strong team: From BDR and marketing to pre-sales and Customer Success, you'll have a strong team behind you, helping you create, close and grow opportunities.

  • A role with real impact: Help shape our UK sales approach, market strategy and way of working as the team and market continue to grow.

  • Awesome office in the heart of London with a dedicated team, combined with travel to clients and the option to work from home.


What you’ll bring:

  • At least five years of work experience, including two years of relevant experience owning a full sales cycle.

  • Experience working in a high-growth environment, preferably in SaaS or a similar context.

  • Experience managing complex decision-making units and closing deals of a comparable size.

title: Director of Quality
description:
About LILT

AI is changing how the world communicates — and LILT is leading that transformation.

We're on a mission to make the world's information accessible to everyone, regardless of the language they speak. We use cutting-edge AI, machine translation, and human-in-the-loop expertise to translate content faster, more accurately, and more cost-effectively without compromising on brand, voice, or quality.

At LILT, we empower our teammates with leading tools, global collaboration, and growth opportunities to do their best work. Our company virtues—Work together, win together; Find a way or make one; Dance in the customer's shoes; Quicker than they expect; Quality is Job 1—guide everything we do. Backed by Sequoia, Intel Capital, and Redpoint, we’re building a category-defining company in a $50B+ global translation market being redefined by AI.

Location: Remote or hybrid, EMEA or US Eastern time zone

Team: Production, Quality

Reports to: VP Production

Direct reports: Quality Manager (AMER, customer staffing) and 2 Quality Coordinators

About the role

As Director of Quality, you will own LILT's quality system end to end: standards, audit, compliance, procedures, continuous improvement, and the roadmap and operation of our Quality Agents. You'll help move Quality from a primarily reactive, execution-led function to a proactive, data-driven partner for customers and internal teams, with quality designed into our AI-native workflows.

You'll be the person who can run a customer audit while simultaneously shipping an improved agent evaluation. As the single Quality partner for Customer Success, Production, Research and Product, you'll turn customer requirements into measurable acceptance criteria, effective controls and better models and workflows. You'll advise customers on the right quality, cost and speed mix, including where automated, agent-verified and human-verified workflows are appropriate, with stronger assurance for high-risk and regulated content.

We're looking for a hands-on Quality SME and operator with real depth in both worlds: experience designing and building AI agents and improving LLM output, and a solid grounding in traditional quality management. You'll bring senior expertise in data, AI, customer advisory and process, and make sure quality work prevents recurrence rather than stopping at rework or ticket closure.

What you'll do

Quality Agent leadership

  • Evaluate, design and build reliable Quality Agents with well-defined tools and clear, structured instructions.

  • Use orchestration patterns to evolve from a single agent to multi-agent systems.

  • Define evaluation criteria, test sets and success metrics for agent performance, and run agents in production with clear monitoring and escalation paths.

  • Drive adoption across teams and show measurable reductions in manual quality effort.

Research and Product partnership

  • Work closely with Research and Product on ADQ, LLM model improvements, AI Review, AI QA, and new and emerging AI workflows.

  • Turn quality findings into product requirements, evaluation criteria and continuous feedback loops that improve model and workflow output.

  • Act as the voice of quality in roadmap discussions, and help decide where human review, AI review or both are needed.

Audit, compliance and procedure

  • Own LILT's approach to internal and external audits, including ISO certification (e.g. ISO 17100, ISO 18587, ISO 9001) and customer audits.

  • Plan and run periodic internal audits, manage evidence collection, and track corrective and preventive actions to closure.

  • Standardise and maintain SOPs, workflows and quality documentation, and keep them current as AI workflows change how we work.

  • Make sure quality processes meet customer, contractual and regulatory requirements.

Customer advisory

  • Partner with Customer Success and Delivery to define proactive quality programmes, success metrics and governance for strategic accounts, including AI-forward enterprise and life science / regulatory programmes.

  • Translate customer quality requirements into clear pre-delivery acceptance criteria, validation methods and risk-appropriate controls.

  • Advise customers on the right quality, cost and speed mix and where automated, agent-verified, human-verified or combined workflows are appropriate.

  • Represent LILT's quality function as a credible subject-matter authority in customer business reviews, audits and escalations, using quality data and metrics to demonstrate fitness for purpose.

Continuous improvement

  • Lead structured CI across the Commercial business: root cause analysis, corrective and preventive actions, KPI reviews and retrospectives.

  • Own a proactive quality metrics framework that makes errors, PQs, rework and trends visible, and use it to prioritise improvements and demonstrate outcomes.

  • Strengthen quality controls across review, delivery and follow-through, including mandatory account-specific checks, intervention on critical findings and clear escalation ownership.

  • Partner with Product and Engineering to automate checks and escalation, and verify that corrective actions prevent recurrence rather than ending at rework or ticket closure.

Expert Operations partnership

  • Partner with Expert Supply and Ops to embed processes, guidance and quality feedback that maintain a high-quality pipeline of experts.

  • Use quality findings and recurring failure patterns to improve expert qualification, guidance and ongoing quality management.

Team leadership

  • Lead and develop the Quality team, including the customer-facing Quality Manager and Quality Coordinators.

  • Establish the team's operating cadence and evolve how the team works as Quality Agents reduce manual coordination work.

  • Oversee embedded Quality Manager staffing sold as a service to customers, ensuring the role owns the specific quality programmes and initiatives those customers pay for.

  • Develop playbooks for AI-driven quality management and keep staffing-as-a-service delivery aligned with LILT's quality standards.

What you'll bring

Must have

  • Agent design and build: demonstrable, hands-on experience designing, building and running LLM-based agents in production. Please be ready to walk us through agents you have built.

  • Data-driven quality management: scripting or data skills (e.g. Python, SQL), with experience turning quality data into actionable metrics, preventive controls and measurable improvements.

  • LLM model improvement: proven experience improving LLM output quality.

  • Significant experience running quality systems, including leading audits (internal and external), compliance programmes, and writing and maintaining processes and procedures. Quality certifications such as Six Sigma are a plus.

  • Experience leading structured CI (RCA, CAPA, KPI reviews).

  • Experience managing and developing people.

  • Customer advisory and cross-functional partnership: a clear communicator who can translate customer quality requirements into acceptance criteria and governance, advise on quality, cost and speed trade-offs, and work credibly with customers, executives and technical teams.

Nice to have

  • Background in localisation, translation or language services.

  • Experience in customer-facing quality roles for enterprise accounts.

  • Research and Product collaboration: a track record of working with research scientists and product managers to turn quality insight into product requirements and shipped improvements.

Our Story

Our founders, Spence and John met at Google working on Google Translate. As researchers at Stanford and Berkeley, they both worked on language technology to make information accessible to everyone. While together at Google, they were amazed to learn that Google Translate wasn’t used for enterprise products and services inside the company.The quality just wasn’t there. So they set out to build something better. LILT was born.

LILT has been a machine learning company since its founding in 2015. At the time, machine translation didn’t meet the quality standard for enterprise translations, so LILT assembled a cutting-edge research team tasked with closing that gap. While meeting customer demand for translation services, LILT has prioritized investments in Large Language Models, human-in-the-loop systems, and now agentic AI.

With AI innovation accelerating and enterprise demand growing, the next phase of LILT’s journey is just beginning.

Our Tech

What sets our platform apart:

  • Brand-aware AI that learns your voice, tone, and terminology to ensure every translation is accurate and consistent

  • Agentic AI workflows that automate the entire translation process from content ingestion to quality review to publishing

  • 100+ native integrations with systems like Adobe Experience Manager, Webflow, Salesforce, GitHub, and Google Drive to simplify content translation

  • Human-in-the-loop reviews via our global network of professional linguists, for high-impact content that requires expert review


LILT in the News

description:

Anthropos is the Enterprise AI transformation platform. We help companies map, verify, and develop the skills of their workforce with AI Simulations, AI Labs, AI Interviews, and our AI Academy. You will be our first marketing hire, and you will own marketing.

There is no playbook to inherit and no team to delegate to on day one. You will work side by side with our CEO and founder and with the sales team, from our offices in Chiasso, and your job is to build the machine that grows our pipeline, our brand, and ultimately our revenue.

This is an operator role, not a strategy-only role. You will write the copy, ship the campaign, run the event, look at the data, and decide what to do next. If that excites you more than managing an agency, keep reading.

What you'll do

  • Demand generation. Design and run campaigns that put qualified enterprise buyers (CHROs, HR and Engineering leaders, CTOs) in front of our sales team. You own the pipeline number with them.
  • SEO and GEO. Grow our organic presence on search engines and inside AI assistants (ChatGPT, Claude, Perplexity). Being found by AI is as important to us as being found by Google, and we are early enough that you can win here.
  • Events. Plan and run our presence at conferences, executive dinners, and our own events, end to end: pick them, organize them, work the room, follow up.
  • Content and brand. Shape how Anthropos sounds and looks in public: website, blog, LinkedIn, email, sales materials. Make the brand feel as good as the product.
  • Measurement. Instrument what you do, report on what worked, kill what didn't, and double down fast.
  • Structure. As things start working, turn them into repeatable processes and eventually into a team you help build.

Who you are

  • An entrepreneur at heart who knows marketing. You treat the function like your own business: you spot opportunities, act without waiting for permission, and own the outcome. Behind that instinct is real experience: years of generalist marketing in startups across demand gen, content, events, and product marketing, so you know which levers actually move pipeline.
  • Someone who gets things done. You are extremely operational. You default to doing, not briefing someone else to do, and you bring results fast. You like being measured on them.
  • An expert with Claude Code, or a heavy daily user of it. We use AI in a very advanced way across the whole company, and we expect marketing to work the same way: producing at a pace and volume a traditional marketer can't match. This is a real requirement, not a nice-to-have.
  • Confident in a startup that moves very fast. We change direction quickly, the bar is high, and some days are stressful. In exchange, you will learn more in a year here than in five anywhere else. You need to genuinely want that trade.
  • A big risk-taker. You launch things that might fail, test channels nobody assigned you, and own the result either way.
  • Not looking for a nine-to-five. This is a startup job, and we are honest about what that means: we work quite a lot. If what you want is a predictable 9-to-5, this is not the right fit, and that's okay. If you want the intensity because of what you get to build, own, and learn, you will feel at home.
  • Fluent in written and spoken English, at a near-perfect level. Most of what you produce will be read by an international audience. Italian is a plus.
  • Able to work from our offices in Chiasso, Ticino. We work in person, with one remote day per week (Thursdays). Relocation support is available where possible.

What you'll get

  • CHF 42,000–50,000 per year, plus a very generous stock package. We'd rather be upfront: this is a startup salary paired with real ownership in the company, and the upside grows with the business you help build.
  • Relocation support, where available, if you are not already in the area.
  • The ability to grow very fast. You start as our first marketing hire; if you deliver, you build and lead the function. No queue of people ahead of you.
  • A direct working relationship with the founder and the sales team: short feedback loops, no layers.
  • The tools to work like it's the AI era: Claude Code, our own platform, and budget for what you need.

How we hire

We use our own product. The process: apply → complete an AI Simulation built for this role → meet the team → offer. It is fast, and you will experience exactly what we sell.

Er zijn over het algemeen drie begeleiders overdag aanwezig en drie a vier in de avond in verband met de zorgbehoefte/zorgvraag van de cliënten. Een aantal cliënten krijgt dagbesteding op de woning. 

Kwadijkerpark 103 bestaat uit een team met een aantal vaste medewerkers die langer op de woongroep werken, met daaromheen zzp’ers en beginnende collega’s. Wij willen ons team uitbouwen met vaste collega’s zodat we onze cliënten meer rust kunnen bieden. We zoeken een collega die weet van doorpakken maar op zijn tijd ook van een geintje houdt. Relativeren in ons vak is belangrijk en daar draagt humor zeker aan bij! In ons team vinden we het belangrijk dat je zegt wat je doet, en doet wat je zegt.
We begeleiden onze cliënten vanuit de onvoorwaardelijke relatie en laten onze cliënten ervaren dat ze mogen zijn wie ze zijn. We zien het als een meerwaarde als je ervaring hebt met onze doelgroep, maar met de juiste motivatie, reflecterend vermogen en passie voor de gehandicaptenzorg ben je ook meer dan welkom om te solliciteren. 

Wat bieden wij?

  • Een brutosalaris tussen € 3.296,00 en €4.705,00 (FWG 50) op basis van een 36-urige werkweek en arbeidsvoorwaarden conform de cao Gehandicaptenzorg;

  • Direct een vast contract. Mogelijkheid tot fiscaal voordelige uitruil van €500 per jaar voor bijvoorbeeld sport of een fiets;

  • Een eindejaarsuitkering (dertiende maand) van 8,33% en 8% vakantiegeld.144 vakantie-uren en 57 uur balansverlof per kalenderjaar op basis van 36 uur;

  • Een onboardingsweek waarin je nieuwe collega’s leert kennen en waardevolle trainingen volgt, om je dienstverband direct goed van start te laten gaan;

  • Een CAO-verhoging van 2% vanaf november;


Wat jij brengt;

Als Senior Regie Begeleider ben je verantwoordelijk voor het opstellen van het ondersteuningsplan en het organiseren, regisseren, evalueren en uitvoeren van de begeleiding en verzorging voor onze cliënten. Je ondersteunt het team in zorgprocessen en coacht en ondersteunt bij het realiseren en coördineren van de afgesproken kwaliteit van zorg. Je houdt de regie in complexe- en crisissituaties en coacht het team waar nodig op cliënt- en teamniveau. Dit alles doe je in nauwe samenwerking met de betrokken gedragskundige en manager.

Met Gentle Teaching als basis biedt je structuur, rust en duidelijke begeleiding. Je stimuleert zelfredzaamheid, motiveert cliënten en brengt een positieve energie mee. 

Je hebt passie voor en bij voorkeur ervaring in het werken met onze doelgroep en de problematiek die onze doelgroep met zich meebrengt. Je bent positief ingesteld, toont lef en maakt er elke dag het beste van!

 

Daarnaast is het belangrijk dat jij:

  • In het bezit bent van een relevant HBO-diploma;

  • Goede communicatieve vaardigheden bezit, zowel professioneel als binnen de driehoek van zorg;

  • Goed in staat bent om te reflecteren op eigen handelen;

  • Beschikt over aanpassings- en relativeringsvermogen;

  • Aantoonbare ervaring hebt in het opstellen, uitvoeren en evalueren van cliëntplannen;

Wat zoeken wij?

Wij zijn op zoek naar een ervaren collega die coach on the job kan bieden en actief meedraait in de diensten. Je weet hoe je beleid en gemaakte afspraken vertaalt naar de dagelijkse praktijk en kunt collega’s ondersteunen bij hulpvragen rondom cliënten, collega’s en verwanten.

Daarnaast verwachten we dat je jezelf binnen afzienbare termijn zodanig bekwaamt dat je:

·        De methodische cyclus op de juiste manier kunt toepassen en, waar nodig, kunt opzetten en structureren.

·        Meerzorgaanvragen kunt opstellen, onderbouwen, op- en afbouwen en evalueren.

·        Wzd-maatregelen kunt opstellen, afbouwen en evalueren.

·        De inzet en bezetting van diensten in kaart kunt brengen en kunt beoordelen of deze passend zijn bij de zorgbehoefte van de cliënten en of er genoeg bezetting is.

·        In staat bent om frictie en spanningen binnen het team te signaleren en hier op een positieve en constructieve manier mee om te gaan, zodat de samenwerking binnen het team wordt versterkt.

·        Beschikt over goede gesprekstechnieken en deze op het juiste moment effectief kunt inzetten.

 

Voor deze rol zoeken we nadrukkelijk een ervaren zorgprofessional. Het is belangrijk dat je voldoende ervaring hebt binnen de zorg en bekend bent met de dynamiek van een team en complexe cliëntsituaties. Deze functie is daarom minder geschikt voor iemand die nog maar kort werkzaam is binnen de zorg.

Samenwerking

Je werkt nauw samen met de betrokken gedragsdeskundige, de regiebegeleiders en het team. Samen zorgen jullie ervoor dat de ondersteuning aan cliënten methodisch, professioneel en passend bij hun zorgbehoefte wordt vormgegeven.

title: Teamleider Instroom & Talentontwikkeling
description:
Bij Prinsenstichting staat een stevige ontwikkeling van de organisatie op stapel. De organisatie verzelfstandigt, de manier van sturen verandert en binnen Mens & Organisatie worden belangrijke stappen gezet om de HR-dienstverlening na verzelfstandiging weer op te bouwen en verder te professionaliseren. Als Teamleider Instroom & Talentontwikkeling krijg jij daarin een sleutelrol.

Je brengt Recruitment, Leren & Ontwikkelen en het Flexbureau dichter bij elkaar en geeft leiding aan professionals die dagelijks werken aan één van de belangrijkste vraagstukken voor Prinsenstichting: zorgen dat de juiste mensen binnenkomen, zich blijven ontwikkelen en op de juiste plek worden ingezet. Je brengt structuur en samenhang, verbetert en ontwikkelt processen en helpt de verschillende disciplines om steeds meer vanuit één gezamenlijke koers te werken.

Een rol waarin je niet in een gespreid bedje terechtkomt, maar juist veel kunt opbouwen. Je combineert mensgericht leiderschap met inhoudelijke stevigheid en krijgt de ruimte om zichtbaar verschil te maken voor medewerkers én voor de zorg aan cliënten.

 

Het aanbod

  • Een jaarsalaris van maximaal € 99.325,- bruto per jaar o.b.v. 36 uur per week inclusief een eindejaarsuitkering van 8,33% en 8% vakantietoeslag.

  • 144 vakantie-uren en 57 uur balansverlof per kalenderjaar bij een fulltime dienstverband.

  • Een dienstverband van 32 – 36 uur.

  • Een contract voor onbepaalde tijd.

  • Deelname aan de pensioenregeling van Pensioenfonds Zorg & Welzijn een verdeling van de premiebetaling tussen werkgever en werknemer.

  • Een vergoeding voor woon-werkverkeer van €0,20 per kilometer en zakelijke reizen  €0,32

  • Jaarlijks de mogelijkheid om bepaalde arbeidsvoorwaarden uit te ruilen (zoals je salaris, vakantietoeslag of eindejaarsuitkering tegen andere kosten bijvoorbeeld voor een sportschool).

  • Ruimte en faciliteiten om werk en privé op een passende manier te combineren, waaronder de mogelijkheid om één dag per week vanuit huis te werken.

 

Jouw kennis en ervaring

  • Je beschikt over hbo/wo werk- en denkniveau en hebt een achtergrond binnen HR/M&O, leren & ontwikkelen en/of organisatieontwikkeling.

  • Je hebt ervaring met het aansturen en ontwikkelen van HR-professionals (functioneel of in projectaansturing) en weet inhoud en leiderschap op een natuurlijke manier te combineren.

  • Je hebt brede affiniteit met de verschillende onderdelen van het vakgebied: leren & ontwikkelen, recruitment, instroom, flexibele inzet en talentontwikkeling.

  • Je beschikt over generalistische HR kennis en hebt aantoonbare ervaring met verander- en professionaliseringsvraagstukken.

  • Je begrijpt wat professioneel leren en ontwikkelen vraagt en kunt meedenken over onder meer leercultuur, opleidingsprogramma's, onboarding en leiderschapsontwikkeling.

  • Ervaring binnen de zorg of gehandicaptenzorg is welkom, maar geen vereiste. Belangrijker is dat je je snel thuis voelt in een complexe, mensgerichte organisatie en begrijpt wat verandering daar vraagt.

 

Hoe ben je succesvol in deze rol?

Je stapt in op een interessant moment. Prinsenstichting verzelfstandigt en verandert de inrichting en besturing van de organisatie. Zelforganisatie maakt plaats voor duidelijker leiderschap, er komt een nieuwe managementstructuur. Per oktober zijn er circa 22 nieuwe Teammanagers aangesteld. Ook binnen M&O worden verantwoordelijkheden opnieuw georganiseerd. Recruitment, Leren & Ontwikkelen, het Flexbureau en de Flexpool worden onder jouw leiding samengebracht.

Daar ligt een stevige ontwikkelopgave. Processen zijn historisch vanuit verschillende onderdelen en locaties ontstaan en kunnen uniformer, slimmer en professioneler worden ingericht. Tegelijkertijd wil je behouden wat waardevol is: betrokken professionals met veel kennis van hun vak, cliënten en organisatie. De kunst is dus niet om alles van bovenaf opnieuw te bedenken, maar om richting te geven, expertise te benutten en samen verbeteringen daadwerkelijk te realiseren. Je kijkt daarbij over de grenzen van de afzonderlijke disciplines heen. Hoe zorg je dat recruitment en opleidingen elkaar nog beter vinden rondom zij-instroom? Hoe ontwikkel je leren van losse scholingsactiviteiten naar een structurele leercultuur? Hoe bouw je de interne flexpool verder uit en verminder je de afhankelijkheid van externe inhuur? En hoe gebruik je data en capaciteitsinformatie om betere keuzes te maken?

Je vertaalt het strategische M&O-beleid naar concrete plannen, processen en resultaten en zorgt er vervolgens voor dat die in de praktijk landen. Daarmee bouw je aan een professionele dienstverlening die de organisatie helpt om ook in een krappe arbeidsmarkt voldoende gekwalificeerde medewerkers aan te trekken, te ontwikkelen en te behouden. Dat sluit rechtstreeks aan bij de formele opdracht om onder meer recruitmentbeleid, opleidingsbeleid, interne mobiliteit, flexpool en capaciteitsplanning verder te ontwikkelen.

Herken jij jezelf hierin?

Je bent koersvast en coachend. Je geeft professionals ruimte en vertrouwen, maar bent duidelijk over de richting en de resultaten die je samen wilt bereiken. Je bent mensgericht en zichtbaar. Je wilt weten wat er binnen je teams en in de organisatie speelt, bent benaderbaar en bouwt gemakkelijk relaties op. Je waardeert de kennis en ervaring die er al is en weet mensen vanuit die basis mee te nemen.
Je bent veranderkundig sensitief. Je begrijpt dat nieuwe structuren en uniforme werkwijzen niet vanzelf worden omarmd. Je kunt omgaan met weerstand, luistert goed naar verschillende perspectieven en houdt tegelijkertijd vast aan wat nodig is.
Je bent inhoudelijk nieuwsgierig en overstijgend. Je hoeft niet op ieder deelgebied de grootste specialist te zijn, maar kunt wel met Recruiters, Opleidingsadviseurs en Planners sparren en ziet de samenhang tussen hun werk.
Je bent besluitvaardig. Je durft het gesprek aan te gaan, echt te luisteren naar wat er speelt en bent vervolgens niet bang om beslissingen te nemen. Ook kun je uitleggen waarom je bepaalde keuzes maakt. Je bent samenwerkingsgericht. Je zoekt actief de verbinding met collega’s en andere disciplines, brengt verschillende perspectieven bij elkaar en werkt vanuit een gezamenlijk belang. Je deelt kennis, benut elkaars expertise en zorgt ervoor dat mensen samen verantwoordelijkheid nemen voor het resultaat. En je bent een bouwer. Je krijgt energie van een omgeving waarin nog niet alles af is. Je brengt structuur, maakt keuzes, zet ideeën om in concrete verbeteringen en neemt mensen daarin mee. Je bent daarbij sterk in het doorgronden, verbeteren en borgen van processen.

 

Jouw verantwoordelijkheden

▪ Je geeft leiding aan de professionals binnen Instroom en Talentontwikkeling, waaronder Recruitment, Leren & Ontwikkelen, het Flexbureau en de Flexpool, en stimuleert samenwerking tussen de verschillende disciplines.

▪ Je vertaalt de M&O-strategie naar meerjaren- en jaarplannen, concrete programma's, processen, doelstellingen en resultaten.

▪ Je ontwikkelt en professionaliseert het beleid en de dienstverlening rond recruitment, arbeidsmarkt, leren & ontwikkelen, interne mobiliteit en flexibele personeelsinzet.

▪ Je bouwt verder aan scholing, een structurele leercultuur en een toekomstbestendig opleidingsportfolio, waaronder ontwikkelpaden, onboarding en leiderschapsontwikkeling.

▪ Je ontwikkelt de interne flexpool verder en stuurt op een effectieve flexibele inzet en vermindering van externe inhuur.

▪ Je brengt meer structuur, uniformiteit en kwaliteit in processen en stimuleert een steeds meer data- en resultaatgerichte manier van werken.

▪ Je adviseert management en organisatie over instroom, ontwikkeling, capaciteit en arbeidsmarktvraagstukken en zorgt dat beleid daadwerkelijk in de praktijk wordt geïmplementeerd.

▪ Je onderhoudt en ontwikkelt relevante externe samenwerkingen, bijvoorbeeld met onderwijsinstellingen, arbeidsmarktpartners en leveranciers.

▪ Je beheert het budget, neemt maatregelen bij afwijkingen en stelt (management) rapportages op.

 

In welk team ga je werken?

Als Teamleider Instroom & Talentontwikkeling geef je leiding aan 5 opleidingsadviseurs, een praktijkbegeleider en 2 administratieve ondersteuners, 3 recruiters, 4 planners en/of administratief medewerkers van het Flexbureau en een Flexpool van circa 20 zorgmedewerkers. Je rapporteert aan de nieuw te werven Manager M&O.

Daarnaast werken er 4 M&O-adviseurs en 3 verzuimadviseurs die rechtstreeks aan de Manager M&O rapporteren. De personeels- en salarisadministratie wordt vanuit een Shared Services Organisatie uitgevoerd. Je rapporteert aan de Manager M&O.

 

De verschillende disciplines beschikken over veel vakkennis en werken met een grote mate van zelfstandigheid en betrokkenheid. Tegelijkertijd is er behoefte aan meer gezamenlijke richting, samenhang en professionalisering. Juist daar voeg jij waarde toe: niet door op de stoel van de specialist te gaan zitten, maar door inhoudelijk een goede gesprekspartner te zijn, prioriteiten te stellen en ervoor te zorgen dat goede ideeën ook worden gerealiseerd.

Je werkt nauw samen met de M&O-adviseurs, de nieuwe teammanagers en het management van Prinsenstichting. Daarmee bevindt jouw team zich op een belangrijk kruispunt in de organisatie: vrijwel alle vraagstukken rondom het vinden, ontwikkelen en flexibel inzetten van medewerkers komen hier samen.

Wat je zeker niet mag missen

Prinsenstichting biedt samen met 1200 zorgprofessionals zorg en ondersteuning aan mensen met een verstandelijke beperking en richt zich steeds nadrukkelijker op cliënten met een complexe en intensieve ondersteuningsvraag. Dat stelt hoge eisen aan de medewerkers die dagelijks naast cliënten staan én aan de manier waarop zij worden geworven, opgeleid en ontwikkeld.

De cultuur is betrokken en sterk cliëntgericht. Veel medewerkers voelen een grote verbondenheid met hun cliënten, collega’s en locatie en werken al lange tijd bij de organisatie. “Prinsenstichting is de thuis van haar cliënten en iedereen draagt eraan bij om hen het leven beter te maken.”Vanaf 1 januari 2027 zal Prinsenstichting zelfstandig verdergaan. Prinsenstichting is nu nog onderdeel van Zorggroep De Opbouw, samen met Silverein en Zideris. In de nieuwe situatie krijgt Prinsenstichting een eigen raad van bestuur en een eigen raad van toezicht. Een deel van de ondersteuning blijft gezamenlijk georganiseerd met de andere twee zorgorganisaties, zodat ondersteunende processen efficiënt geregeld blijven. De verzelfstandiging heeft geen direct effect op de dagelijkse zorg voor cliënten: die gaat door met dezelfde aandacht, kwaliteit en betrokkenheid bij cliënten en hun naasten. Tegelijkertijd maakt de zelfstandige positie het gemakkelijker om snel in te spelen op veranderingen en kansen in de zorg en om de samenwerking in de regio te intensiveren. Dat is belangrijk nu zorgvragen complexer worden en het vinden van voldoende goede collega’s uitdagend blijft. Door de historie van autonomie en zelforganisatie zijn verschillen ontstaan in werkwijzen tussen teams en locaties. De organisatie kiest nu bewust voor meer duidelijkheid, professioneel leiderschap, samenhang en uniformiteit. Dat maakt deze functie bijzonder. Er ligt veel om op voort te bouwen, maar ook veel om te ontwikkelen. Voor iemand die energie krijgt van bouwen, verbinden en professionaliseren, biedt Prinsenstichting daardoor veel ruimte om daadwerkelijk iets neer te zetten.

De procedure

Bureau Blaauw verzorgt de externe search en voorselectie, inclusief het eerste interview. Ook interne kandidaten worden in het proces meegenomen en langs dezelfde criteria beoordeeld als externe kandidaten.

Kandidaten die worden meegenomen in de verdere selectieprocedure bij Prinsenstichting, voeren gesprekken met een adviescommissie en een selectiecommissie. In beide commissies zijn vertegenwoordigers vanuit M&O betrokken.

Bij een positieve afronding van de gesprekken volgt een arbeidsvoorwaardelijk voorstel.

De volgende stap nemen?

Stuur ons je CV en korte motivatie uiterlijk 16 oktober 2026. Neem gerust contact op met onze consultants als je vragen hebt.

Daniëlle van der Vegt

Ilonka van Dijk

title: Accounting Employee (senior)
description:
Do you want to play a key role in keeping our financial administration sharp, while helping accelerate the energy transition?

Join FincoEnergies as Accounting Employee in the Road & Marine division. In this role, you will ensure flawless financial administration across multiple entities and you will be key to accurate and timely reporting. This includes daily financial operations as well as monthly and period-end closing activities, including reconciliations and checks in the accounting system to ensure accurate, complete, and timely financial reporting. You will become part of the Road & Marine finance team based in Rotterdam and report directly to the Teamlead Accounting. Together, you will help shape the future of sustainable transport solutions.

Your responsibilities as (senior) Accounting Employee

  • Handle daily financial operations: process purchase, sales, and bank transactions, and validate invoices for accuracy.

  • Posting invoices to the appropriate cost centers, responding to supplier inquiries, and managing internal recharges.

  • Acounts receivable and payable overdue reporting and follow-up.

  • Contribute to month- and year-end close, reporting and audits, including booking accruals, preparation of balance sheet files, assisting in VAT filings and explaining results.

  • Coordinating with commericial backoffice and finance departments within the division and the FincoEnergies group.

 

Your Talents

  • Understanding how accounting activities and decisions impact financial reporting and the wider business.

  • Actively building and maintaining knowledge and experience, sharing and developing expertise, with ambition and flexibility correlating to experience.

  • Adapting communication and working style to different stakeholders and situations while maintaining focus on objectives.

  • Proficiency in addressing urgent issues and overcoming obstacles through creative solutions or collaborations to achieve set goals.

  • Maintaining a strong focus on both goal achievement and process quality to attain the desired results.

As our new Front Runner you bring

  • A higher educational level (HBO) or working level;

  • 5+ years of work experience in a similar role;

  • A result-driven, enthusiastic, proactive, and accurate mindset;

  • Proficiency in Dutch and English, both spoken and written. Applications will only be considered if both language requirements are met;

  • Experience preparing VAT returns and performing month-end closing activities;

  • Strong knowledge of Microsoft Excel, including PivotTables and VLOOKUP.

  • Experience with ERP systems - experience with Microsoft Business Central and Blue10 is considered a plus.

  • Knowledge of and experience in trading organisations, especially in fuels or energy is a significant plus.


  • A strong salary based on experience & competencies and attractive yearly bonus potential;

  • 8% holiday allowance;

  • A collective pension plan with two-thirds covered by FincoEnergies;

  • A yearly budget of € 900,- gross for your well-being and development;

  • An annual training budget of € 2000,- gross to support your professional development;

  • 25 vacation days (based on full-time employment);

  • Flexible & remote work (>60% in the office);

  • Entrepreneurial and sustainable environment providing growth and development opportunities;

We're looking for an HPC & Compute Infrastructure Engineer to own the compute infrastructure behind our metrology equipment and our development environment, from hardware specification and system build-up to performance and supplier management.

Our measurements are reconstructed from raw data using physics-based models and inverse-problem algorithms, which makes our software stack a demanding, GPU-heavy scientific computing workload. Our Algorithm Architect and Software Architect define what the stack needs in throughput and compute; you turn those needs into concrete hardware, build it up and keep it running.

The role is broad, covering both the compute that is part of our product and the infrastructure we run in-house. You'll be the technical lead towards our suppliers, while staying hands-on yourself.

•     Own the HPC and compute infrastructure for both our product and our in-house environment: set direction, make design decisions and keep it running

•     Act as technical lead towards suppliers: evaluate options, challenge proposals, and follow deliveries through to installation and acceptance

•     Work with the algorithm and software teams to understand how the stack uses its compute, and find where performance can be gained on the hardware side

•     Set up and maintain the tooling around the infrastructure, such as provisioning, monitoring and job scheduling

•     Support the installation of product compute at customer sites, working within customer IT and security requirements

•     Grow into adjacent responsibilities as the team scales, such as capacity planning and budget input

Is this you?

•     A degree in computer science, computer engineering or a related field (or equivalent experience), with at least 5 years of experience in HPC or compute infrastructure

•     A track record of designing and building up HPC or compute infrastructure, taking it from specification to a running system

•     Hands-on experience with Linux systems, GPU or accelerator hardware, high-speed networking and storage, and tools such as Slurm, Ansible or containers

•     Active use of AI tooling in your daily work (scripting, automation, monitoring, troubleshooting, documentation) to boost efficiency

•     A self-driven attitude and comfort with owning a broad area, with a startup mindset and the curiosity to dig into the software stack that runs on your hardware

Nice to have

•     Experience running GPU-accelerated scientific or numerical workloads, such as simulation or model-based reconstruction

•     Experience with low-latency interconnects such as InfiniBand or RDMA

•     Experience with Kubernetes or other container orchestration

•     A background in semiconductor equipment, or in compute integrated into industrial or high-tech systems

What We Offer

•     A role at the heart of Invisix's compute infrastructure, with real technical ownership from day one

•     Competitive salary and benefits, including an Employee Share Ownership Plan

•     A learning and development budget to support your growth

•     Flexible working arrangements, and room to grow into adjacent responsibilities as the team scales

Interested?

title: Finance Lead (w/d/m)
description:
Über LIFTED

LIFTED is a strength training company from Berlin. We run six studios across the city and plan to have 20 by the end of 2027, with Munich, Hamburg, Cologne and Düsseldorf next. Our goal is to become the largest fitness company in Europe. Before LIFTED, the founding team helped build and scale BEAT81. Today we’re profitable and owner-led.

Why this role exists
Today Carl, one of the founders, runs finance alongside managing the company, with bookkeeping at an external tax firm. You take this over and build out the finance function.


What you own

  • Finance ops. You lead our finance trainee, who handles receipts, invoices and account coding based on clear rules. You review samples, resolve new cases and adapt the rules. You also manage payments, payroll and the month-end and year-end close with our tax firm.

  • Planning and liquidity. You own our planning model, plan liquidity monthly, and run the annual budget, forecasts and scenarios. Before we sign a new location, you build its business case and add it to the planning model.

  • Reporting. You set up monthly management reporting that we use in the management meeting.

  • Financing. You prepare our financing and, over time, lead parts of the conversations with our financing partners.

  • HR admin. You handle employee data and contracts. Right now that’s a few hours a month.

  • Team. You build the finance team and help us decide when HR needs its own role.

How we measure success

  • After 3 months, you’ve taken over finance from Carl, from daily operations and HR admin to planning and liquidity.

  • After 6 months, management reporting runs every month. You’ve built the business cases for the locations we signed in that time and prepared your first financing.

  • After 12 months, you run the annual budget, align it with the team leads and review it with us every quarter. You prepare our financing end to end and lead parts of the conversations with our financing partners yourself.


What you bring
You might have done most of this before, or you’re ready to grow into it.

  • Around 4–6 years in finance, including experience at a startup or scale-up

  • A strong academic background in business, finance or a similar field

  • Experience with month-end closes and working with an external tax firm

  • Experience building or fundamentally rebuilding a planning model in spreadsheets

  • Sound understanding of account coding

  • You want to understand how a studio makes money and use the numbers to shape decisions with us

  • Fluent German, English C1

  • You live in Berlin or are moving here, and work with us in the office

  • Hands-on with getting-things-done mentality

Nice to have:

  • Experience in a fast-growing business with multiple locations

  • Experience preparing financing, for example bank or development loans

  • Experience with SKR03, DATEV, Moss, Helu or similar tools

  • First leadership experience

What we offer

  • The chance to build our finance team

  • You work directly with Carl, who coaches you on the business side, from location decisions to financing

  • A spacious and bright office at Senefelder Platz, between Mitte and Prenzlauer Berg

  • Free, unlimited membership at all LIFTED studios

  • Team events like padel and BBQs

How to apply
No cover letter needed. Send us your CV with a short note (3–5 sentences) about something in finance you built or changed yourself: What was the problem, what did you do, and what changed afterwards?

title: Senior Thermomechanical Analysis Engineer – Extreme Environments (all genders)
description:
Your Mission:

As Senior Thermomechanical Analysis Engineer (all genders) you will join VÆRIDION’s Technology division within the Mechanical Design & Integration team and lead the structural, stress, and thermomechanical finite element analysis (FEA) of the propulsion battery system for VÆRIDION’s CS-23 all-electric aircraft.

You will own the computational modelling of battery packs, power distribution units (PDUs), and their internal hardware, predicting how every component behaves under nominal and emergency conditions – including thermal runaway, the DO-160 environmental qualification conditions applied to the pack and PDU as airborne equipment (temperature and altitude, temperature variation, humidity, operational shocks and crash safety, and vibration), flight loads, and durability over service life. Your analysis will provide engineering evidence that the propulsion battery system is structurally robust, thermally safe, and certifiable.

Within the Mechanical Design & Integration team, you will collaborate with Mechanical Design, Materials & Processes, Test, HV Electrical Systems, Airborne Electronics, Thermal Systems, Aircraft Structures, Certification, Safety, and Quality teams to define analysis methods, apply the material property allowable required for your analyses, and substantiate the qualification of the propulsion battery pack and PDU. You will be the structural and thermomechanical analysis authority for the propulsion battery system, responsible for checking and releasing design against the applicable stress and thermomechanical requirements.

Your work will directly contribute to the propulsion battery system that underpins VÆRIDION’s mission to bring electric flight to regional aviation.

 

Your Day-to-Day:

  • Lead the structural, stress, and thermomechanical FEA of propulsion battery packs, PDUs, and their internal components, predicting how they behave under nominal operation and emergency conditions – including thermal runaway, the DO-160 environmental qualification conditions, and flight and inertial loads.

  • Perform room-temperature and elevated-temperature analysis of composites (including sandwich structures), metals, adhesives, and mechanical fasteners, capturing temperature-dependent material behaviour.

  • Assess creep and stress relaxation of seals, adhesives, polymers, potting compounds, and thermal interface materials at elevated temperature, including loss of contact pressure across a pack replacement interval.

  • Analyse thermal runaway response as a coupled thermomechanical event – pressure loads, direct impingement flow, ejecta, and heat transfer to surrounding structure and systems – working closely with the Thermal Systems team on thermal runaway CFD modelling and the resulting heat transfer boundary conditions, in support of containment and continued safe flight and landing.

  • Apply static, fatigue, and creep material property allowable (room and elevated temperature) in the substantiation of the propulsion battery pack and PDU, working to established methodologies such as CMH-17 for composites and MMPDS for metallics, and specify the allowable, material data, and test conditions required from the Materials & Processes and Test teams.

  • Automate and script analysis workflows – model generation, parametric studies, load case sweeps, and post-processing – using Python for Abaqus scripting, and develop closed-form and lower-order analysis methods in Python or MATLAB to size hardware quickly and to verify finite element results.

  • Interface closely with the Mechanical Design, Materials & Processes, and Airborne Electronics teams to translate analysis results into design improvements and robust, certifiable hardware.

  • Check and release design against the applicable stress and thermomechanical requirements, providing the stress sign-off for propulsion battery pack and PDU hardware releases.

  • Define modelling standards, assumptions, load cases, and acceptance criteria, and maintain configuration-controlled analysis models and inputs.

  • Support test planning and post-test correlation of FEA models against coupon, component, and full-scale test data.

  • Author and release certification documentation, including analysis reports and means-of-compliance evidence for structural, environmental, and thermal runaway requirements.

 

Your Profile:

  • 5+ years of experience in structural/stress and thermomechanical FEA, preferably in aerospace, automotive, battery systems, or other high-performance engineering environments.

  • Experience taking analytical responsibility for hardware, including checking the work of others and providing stress sign-off or equivalent release approval within a configuration-controlled environment, is desirable.

  • Strong command of nonlinear FEA across material, geometric, and contact nonlinearity, with depth in several of the following: cohesive-zone modeling with traction–separation, composite progressive failure (e.g., Hashin/Puck), metal plasticity and viscoplasticity, hyperelastic and viscoelastic materials, crushable foam plasticity, large-deformation and buckling, and frictional contact with pretension, including fastener bearing and bearing–bypass analysis.

  • Experience with room-temperature and elevated-temperature modeling of composites (including sandwich structures), metals, adhesives, and mechanical fasteners, covering temperature-dependent material behavior.

  • Experience implementing user-defined material models and subroutines in Abaqus (UMAT/VUMAT/UMATHT), including the ability to write and debug Fortran, is desirable.

  • Proficiency in scripting: Python for Abaqus automation and post-processing, and Python or MATLAB for closed-form and lower-order analysis methods used to size hardware and verify finite element results.

  • Proficiency with 3D CAD, ideally SolidWorks or CATIA, is desirable; experience with Siemens NX is beneficial.

  • Experience applying static, fatigue, and creep material property allowables to the substantiation of structural hardware, including familiarity with CMH-17 and MMPDS methodologies or equivalent, and with A-/B-basis statistical allowables.

  • Familiarity with aerospace environmental and structural requirements, in particular DO-160 environmental conditions and CS-23 structural substantiation, is desirable.

  • Experience with battery systems or electric propulsion systems is beneficial.

title: Senior People Partner
description:
Senior People Partner

Cloudscaler | London | People Team | Reports to the Chief People Officer | £55,000–£75,000

Someone has to own the People initiative that doesn’t fit neatly into anyone’s week and the case nobody else should be handling. That someone is you — not as an escalation point, but as the person who runs the day-to-day of this function.

THE MOMENT

Cloudscaler is 130 people today. We’ll be 170 by the end of this year, and roughly double again in 2027. The People function is being built in real time alongside that growth, rather than inherited from someone who left years ago.

You’ll be the first hire into the People team. For roughly your first year you’ll be the only People professional alongside the CPO, which means running the whole day-to-day of the function: the hardest casework and initiatives, and the operational core that keeps everything moving. A People Partner is planned to join later in 2027, and at that point the operational administration moves to them.

This is also a role built with room to grow. As the team expands beyond that second hire, we expect this role to take on day-to-day operational leadership of the People Partner practice, but that isn’t the shape of it on day one.

WHAT MAKES THIS DIFFERENT

In most People teams, the senior generalist is just a People Partner with a harder case queue. Here, the difference is ownership, not just difficulty.

  • Complex casework: Rather than simply handling harder cases, you’ll own the most complex cases end to end, with no hand back.

  • People initiatives: Rather than contributing to initiatives someone else drives, you’ll own them from design through to embedding.

  • Decision-making: Rather than escalating ambiguity upward, you’ll make the sensible call and document your reasoning.

  • CPO partnership: Rather than acting in a support role to the CPO, you’ll be an operational partner they can confidently delegate to.

To be clear about the level: The CPO still designs the People strategy and the systems architecture. You own how it runs day to day, and you’re trusted to run a whole initiative, not just a case. That is a different job to People Partner, not a bigger version of the same one.

THE ROLE

You’ll sit in the People team reporting to the Chief People Officer. Three strands make up the job:

  • Casework: The employee relations situations with the most complexity or sensitivity land with you, start to finish.

  • Initiatives: When the CPO needs a piece of work owned (a policy rollout, a wellbeing programme, a piece of the reward or benefits agenda), you take it from design through to something that runs.

  • Operations: Until the People Partner joins, you’ll own payroll and benefits administration, onboarding, screening and security clearances, and keeping Rippling accurate.

When the People Partner joins, they’ll report to the CPO. You won’t manage them formally, but you’ll lead their handover, you’ll be the person they come to first, and your judgement will set the standard for how this function operates day to day.

WHERE THE ROLE STARTS AND STOPS

New roles get vague, so here is the boundary as we see it today.

Yours

  • The most complex and sensitive employee relations casework, end to end.

  • Full ownership of People initiatives, from design to embedding.

  • Acting as the CPO’s operational partner on ambiguous or cross-cutting problems.

  • Until the People Partner joins (planned for later in 2027):

    • Payroll and benefits administration, including the monthly payroll cycle in Rippling and Mintago.

    • Pre-onboarding, onboarding and probation.

    • Background screening in Zinc.

    • Security clearance coordination.

    • Rippling data quality, workflows and reporting.

    • Our working groups and committees.

  • Once the People Partner joins:

    • A structured handover of the operational core.

    • Day-to-day guidance for the People Partner.

Shared

  • Ashby, which Talent Acquisition owns. You’ll work in it from offer through to start date on every hire until the People Partner joins, and on senior hires after that.

  • Mentoring and supporting the People Partner on their casework and initiatives, once they join.

Not yours

  • Recruitment delivery, which sits with Talent Acquisition.

  • The design of the People strategy, the operating model and the systems architecture, which sit with the CPO.

  • Formal line management of the People Partner, who will report to the CPO.

THE STACK

  • Rippling: Our single source of truth. Until the People Partner joins you’ll run it day to day, including the monthly payroll cycle, data quality and workflows, and you’ll use its reporting at a level that supports whole initiatives.

  • Zinc: Background screening. You’ll run checks for every new joiner until the People Partner joins, and stay close to the senior and sensitive hires after that.

  • Ashby: Owned by Talent Acquisition. You’ll work in it from offer through to start date on the hires you’re responsible for.

  • Claude: A daily tool here. You’ll use it for casework preparation, drafting policy and communications, and pulling together the analysis behind an initiative.

  • Mintago: Our employee benefits and financial wellbeing platform (pensions, salary sacrifice and financial advice). You’ll administer it and keep enrolment accurate until the People Partner takes it on.

WHAT YOU’LL DO

  • Own the hardest casework. You’ll run our most complex and sensitive employee relations cases end to end, with the CPO there to sense-check rather than take over.

  • Own initiatives, not tasks. You’ll take a People initiative from a rough brief to something that’s running and embedded, rather than handing it back once the interesting part is done.

  • Run the operational core. Until the People Partner joins, you’ll own the monthly payroll cycle in Rippling, benefits administration including Mintago, onboarding, background screening and security clearances. Accurate, on time, and documented as you go.

  • Hand it over well. When the People Partner arrives, you’ll give them a working system and a clear handover, then stay the person they come to first and the judgement others in the function measure themselves against.

  • Partner with senior leaders. You’ll be credible with leaders on the most difficult conversations: complex change, capability, and situations without a clean playbook.

  • Use AI properly. You’ll use Claude daily to take time out of your own week, checking anything that touches a decision about a person and owning the outcome.

  • Improve what you find. You’ll spot the gaps in policy, process or practice before anyone else does, and bring the CPO a considered view on the fix, not just the problem.

WHAT SUCCESS LOOKS LIKE AT 12 MONTHS

  • You’re running the most complex ER cases with confidence, and the CPO isn’t being pulled into them.

  • At least one or two People initiatives have gone from a rough brief to something genuinely embedded, owned by you.

  • Payroll, benefits, onboarding and clearances run accurately and on time, and every process is documented well enough to hand over.

  • You’ve helped shape the People Partner hire, so the handover is ready when they land.

  • Senior leaders treat you as a credible operational partner, not an escalation point.

  • You’ve made and documented sensible calls in genuinely ambiguous situations, and they’ve held up.

  • The CPO can hand you an ambiguous problem and trust it gets shaped properly.

WHO WE’RE LOOKING FOR

  • Deep employee relations experience. You’ve run complex disciplinaries, grievances and change situations yourself, and you know exactly when to escalate and when not to. CIPD qualification, or solid progress towards it, is welcome.

  • A track record of owning initiatives. You can point to work you took from a brief to something that actually ran, not just a project you contributed to.

  • Hands-on with the operational detail. You’ve owned or closely supported a payroll cycle, benefits administration and onboarding, and you’re comfortable being accountable for their accuracy while also carrying the senior work.

  • Credible with senior leaders. You can hold your own in a difficult conversation with someone under real pressure and be listened to.

  • Comfortable operating near-autonomously. You don’t need a playbook for everything. You make a sensible call, write it down, and check it with the CPO afterwards.

  • Ready to grow into people leadership. You won’t formally manage anyone at the start, but you’ll induct and guide the People Partner when they join, and you should want to lead a team as the structure catches up.

  • Discreet and organised at volume. Complex casework and live initiatives, often at the same time. You’ll need a system, and it can’t be your memory.

THE HONEST PART

This role sits in an odd space for now: senior in scope and judgement, without a team underneath it yet. Until the People Partner joins later in 2027, you’ll also be the whole operational team, so a payroll deadline and a complex grievance can land in the same week. That eases as the function grows, but it means the authority you carry day to day has to come from the quality of your work, not a job title.

You are not designing the People strategy or the systems architecture. The CPO does that. What you get instead is real ownership of the hardest cases and the initiatives that matter, a close working relationship with the CPO, and a genuine path toward leading the People Partner practice as it grows.

This probably isn’t for you if you want a formal team from day one, or if you’d rather leave payroll and onboarding to someone else. It probably is for you if you want to prove you can run this function well enough, top to bottom, that a team gets built around you.

If that sounds like the challenge you’ve been looking for, let’s talk.

title: Head of Data & Intelligence
description:
Creandum's edge has always been people: the network, the judgment, the hustle. To sharpen our edge, we need to make everything those people learn compound: every meeting, every diligence process, every founder relationship feeding a shared foundation instead of evaporating into inboxes and individual heads.

You will build and own that foundation: the firm's data platform, the intelligence layer on top of it, and the governance that makes partners willing to trust it with their most sensitive work.

This is a new function, and you are its first hire. You'll start hands-on-keyboard and stay that way for the time being; but you're building an estate the firm will run on, and the mandate grows with what you prove.

You report to the Operating Partner, but work directly and independently with every member of the firm.

We believe different viewpoints drive our growth, and we welcome applicants from all backgrounds.

What you'll own

The data platform. The firm's data architecture end to end: warehouse, ingestion from core systems (CRM, meeting transcripts, documents, email/calendar), entity resolution, and data quality. One person, one company, one deal – consistent across every source. This is foundational; everything else flows from it.

The intelligence layer. Retrieval, search & agent tooling that give everyone's AI real firm context, serving both individual workflows (bottom-up) and firm-wide platforms (top-down). Built for passive compounding: the system gets better as people work and as models improve, without depending on anyone's discipline.

Access, trust, and AI risk. The access model as structural enforcement, not instructions: who sees what, with identity, provenance, and audit. Sensitive fund and partner data protected to a standard the partnership will trust, plus the AI-specific risk judgment (injection containment, egress, tool guardrails) for everything the function ships, in collaboration with legal/regulatory counsel.

Technology strategy and the tool estate. Accountability for whether the firm's tools are the right ones: evaluation, integration, and replacement of the systems and data sources the firm runs on, in close partnership with the stakeholders who use them. Buy when buying is better; build when building is better. You have the mandate to choose, and then execute on your decision. Make sure security, compliance and budget are part of the equation.

What you'll deliver

First 6 months. A complete map of the firm's data and systems. The foundational data platform stood up. Two or three lightweight tools shipped that visibly improve how a team works. A clear, prioritized 12–18 month roadmap, authored by you and agreed with the partnership.

By 12 months. V1 of the firm's shared intelligence layer live and in daily use. The diligence process made genuinely multiplayer; firm knowledge and meeting history informing live deals instead of sitting unused. Measurable adoption, reported honestly, with failures killed as quickly as the wins are shipped.

Beyond. The roadmap is yours to define. Candidates for the frontier: productizing how the firm wins deals, network intelligence that answers "who do we know" in seconds, platform tools founders can self-serve, and operational automation across finance, events, and admin.

How you'll work

  • Builder first. You ship personally. This is not a role for someone who wants a team of ten doing the building.

  • Co-creation, not solo genius. Stakeholders across the firm (investment, platform, marketing, operations, etc.) steer, test, and tune what you build. Within a year, everyone at the firm should be able to point at something they had a hand in shaping.

  • Product discipline. Prototype, validate with real users, kill what doesn't get adopted. Usage is the metric; expect and budget for churn.

  • Scale deliberately. You start solo. As the foundation proves out, you'll orchestrate internal or external build resources and potentially grow the function. You are prepared to identify, leverage and lead exceptional talent to help achieve results.

Who you are

  • You've shipped a real data or AI product end to end (pipelines, retrieval, and the product surface) and people actually used it.

  • Deep, hands-on command of data architecture, warehousing, and governance. Fluent with embeddings, retrieval, and agents that act, not just answer.

  • You treat access control and provenance as product features, not compliance chores.

  • Low ego, high agency, energized by a blank page. Excited to tackle the unglamorous work (entity resolution, data hygiene, permissions) that everything depends on.

  • You can sit with an investor, an EA, and a founder in the same week and design for all of them. Venture experience isn't required, but you'll need to earn a front-line view of the work fast.

  • You can say "no" and "not yet" to smart, senior people and make them glad you did.

What this role is not

  • Not IT operations: endpoint, device & office infrastructure are handled by our managed IT partner.

  • Not reg compliance: policy & DORA workstreams are owned by legal, with your input on anything AI.

  • Not a reporting function: you build systems that answer questions, not dashboards on request.

Why this role

You'll have a blank page, real budget influence, direct partnership access, and a firm small enough that what you build touches everyone within weeks. The firms that figure this out will compound differently from the ones that don't. This is the seat where that happens.

title: Founding Engineer (Remote or Hybrid - EEA/UK)
description:
Founding Engineer


Role can be based remotely in the EEA or hybrid in our London or Munich offices.

Fixed software is the wrong shape for logistics, because every team runs its processes differently. Tare is our solution. Combining agentic AI with deterministic logic means Tare fits to any customer but runs the same way every single time. We have just closed our pre-seed funding round with a top European VC and we are now looking for a founding engineer to build Tare with us.

About Tarebase

We're Dom and Felix, the two co-founders of Tarebase. Dom is a former SVP at a global unicorn, overseeing tens of millions in global carrier spend, with deep logistics domain experience from Amazon, Nestle and EY. Felix was a founding engineer at Raycast and has spent more than two decades building software systems. We've raised pre-seed funding from a top-tier European VC and are building our MVP together with early design partners, who will become our first customers. As our first employee, you'd have a real say in both the product and the engineering decisions behind it.

Logistics is difficult to run well, and experienced people are hard to hire. Smaller businesses often pay too much for shipping, struggle to give customers a good delivery experience, and can't match larger competitors' technology or hiring budgets. The software available to them is often expensive, dated or too cumbersome. We want to make logistics less of a burden so these businesses can spend more time selling their products.They're the customers we want to build for: Europe alone has around 26 million SMEs, employing more than 100 million people.

Just putting a chat interface and GPT-wrapper on top of the problem is not what we're building. We're combining extraction and analysis, workflow automation, agentic and compiled AI with deterministic, verifiable logic. Recent advances in AI make more of this possible, but building a system that does it reliably is still hard. We're looking for someone who wants to advance the state of the art in this area with us.

About you

The description below is an ideal, not a checklist. If you don't tick every box but feel ready for the challenges of being the first engineer at an early-stage startup, we'd still like to hear from you. What matters most to us is that you're motivated, committed, willing to stick with hard problems, and someone we can count on.

You have a strong technical background and a track record of building and shipping software systems, whether that's cloud backends, web applications, AI-supported systems or a mix of these. You enjoy working across engineering and product. You think like a product engineer: you care about UX/UI, and you want direct contact with customers and the people who use what you build.

You'll work mostly in Rust and TypeScript, across the full stack: data engineering, AI, backend, frontend, infrastructure and deployment. We especially value experience with either language from before AI coding tools and a solid understanding of its ecosystem so you can make considered choices. We also value experience operating distributed systems and data-intensive systems in the cloud, including multi-tenant environments and the scaling and security challenges they bring, databases, and durable execution runtimes.

You use coding agents effectively, but stay close to the code. You know their limitations in a large codebase, review and challenge their work, and take testing, debugging, refactoring and documentation seriously. You can design useful tests and evaluations, manage complexity, and tell when something is genuinely ready to ship.

You also enjoy digging into challenging problems. You keep up with what current models, agent harnesses and research make possible, and you can judge what actually works for a given use case. You know how to build agents and AI workflows into a product and use evaluations, validation and deterministic logic to make what they produce consistent and verifiable. You're comfortable extracting structure from messy documents and care a lot about data quality. You experiment, measure the results, question your assumptions, and keep going until you've found a solution that really holds up.

You can turn that work into shipped software, taking a product idea or technical direction through design and implementation without waiting for someone to assign you a ticket. We work remotely, so clear communication and follow-through matter a lot to us. We value people who manage their own work, can be counted on, and raise important issues early.

How to apply

Apply with the button on this page.

Please ensure to use a hand-written CV. We read every application ourselves. It's fine to use tools for spelling or translation, but we want to hear your voice.

Our process

The process should take a few weeks from start to finish depending on your availability.

  1. Application review. If we love your resume we will send over some short questions.

  2. Intro call with Dom and Felix. An informal conversation about the role, the technology and what you're looking for.

  3. Technical deep dive with Felix. We talk briefly about a system you’ve worked on (no need to share anything confidential), then work through a system design problem together.

  4. Half a day with us in Munich or London. We cover your travel, hotel if needed, and meals. You spend about two hours on a made-up task similar to the problems we work on, using your usual tools and coding agents. Then we have lunch, go through your work together, and talk through a customer scenario.

  5. References and offer. We speak with 1-2 people you've worked with (only with your agreement) and aim to decide within 48 hours.

If we don't move forward after the technical conversation or later, we'll share some feedback with you.

Compensation: €100.000–120.000 base salary plus 0.75–1% equity

Setup: A MacBook Pro and whatever else you need to work well. If you'd rather not work from home, we'll pay for a coworking space near you.

Location: Munich or London, or remote within Europe (GMT-1 to GMT+3) with regular meet-ups.

title: Senior Product Analyst (w/m/d)
description:
Deine Aufgaben
